subject: Turtle WoW Unique Items
content_md:
Turtle WoW is unique not only because of its expansion content, but also because of its ability to create unique assets never before made available for players to obtain. author: Dragunovi
subject: Introduction and Fundamentals
content_md:
Greetings and welcome to the Itemization section of the Turtle WoW Forum! Here you will find dedicated forum posts that give details on additions, changes and reworks done on different parts of Turtle WoW. From massive profession craft revamps to new recipe additions, you can find details for it all here.

Now that the introduction is out of the way, I'll get into the Fundamentals. These changes and additions are deep rooted and their effects can be found in many parts of itemization and the game as a whole.

 **Reminder that anything slated to be added or changed is subject to change before release.**

 **New Stats:**
- **1.16.0:**  Haste: You can find this effect listed as "Increases your attack and casting speed by X%.". This effect passively increases you attack and casting speed, useful for classes that rely more on weapon and item procs on hit such as hybrids and dual wielding classes.

- **1.16.0:**  Meditation: You can find this effect listed as "Allows X% of your Mana regeneration to continue while casting.". Useful for most mana related classes, but especially Druids and Priests which have spirit in their Tier Sets and spirit related talents.

- **1.16.1:**  Armor Penetration: You can find this effect listed as "Your attacks ignore X of the target's armor.". Primarily for physical damage dealers, its effect snowballs as the enemy takes more and more damage with less armor, especially powerful if the target has armor reducing effects in a raid environment to stack the stat with.

- **1.17.0:**  Regeneration: You can find this effect listed as "Allows X% of your Health regeneration to work while in combat.". Especially useful for classes without self healing capabilities, allowing health sustain in combat.

- **1.17.0:**  Vampirism: You can find this effect listed as "% of your damage is returned as healing." which is pretty self explanatory, especially useful for outdoor content. Primarily found in Gilneas as the source of the magic for the lifestealing effects originate from it.

- **1.17.0:**  Resillience: You can find this effect listed as "Reduces your chance to get critically hit by X%". Currently only found in set bonuses for PvP sets, a few items in the Lower Karazhan Halls and a few other miscellaneous sources.
 **General Adjustments:**

- **1.16.0:** The stat budget for Health every 5 seconds (HP5) is massively reduced, its now mainly used for flavor purposes due to how weak it is and items that have had this stat in Vanilla have seen some slight buffs in compensation.

- **1.17.0:** Increased Chance to Parry stat cost has been decreased from **15.65 to 13.35**.

This essentially means items with parry now have room for a bit more stats. Parry Haste was valued too much compared to Dodge where the Increased Parry got its extra cost. We hope this makes the stat more viable to use in gearing without sacrificing too many other stats.
This change affects **40+ items**, we won't list all changes here for that reason, but you can expect small to medium increases in other stats the item utilizes depending on the amount of parry stat.

- **1.17.0:** Most Two-Handed Maces and Polearms now grant Feral Attack Power, granting 14 for every item level above 60.
Below are a few examples and not an extensive list of all weapons with Feral AP:

- Bonecrusher: 42 Feral AP

- Unyielding Maul: 28 Feral AP

- Boneshatter Maul: 70 Feral AP

- Nat Pagle's Fish Terminator: 70 Feral AP

- Finkle's Lava Dredger: 140 Feral AP

- Herald of Woe: 210 Feral AP

- Barb of the Sand Reaver: 238 Feral AP

- R14 PvP Polearms: 252 Feral AP

- Eye of Nerub: 322 Feral AP

- **Pre-1.15.0** All skills including Polearms can now be learned at Level 5. Polearm learning cost has been reduced to 10 Silver.

- **1.16.0:** Shamans can now learn Two-Handed Mace and Axe skills and the ability to Parry from trainers and no longer require a talent in the Enhancement tree to do so.

- **1.17.0:** Druids can now learn the Polearm skill from trainers.

- **1.17.0::** Polearms below Item Level 25 had their level requirements adjusted to be usable at a lower level. Back in Vanilla all polearms had to have a level requirement of 20 at minimum regardless of item level due to the skill learning level and no race starting with the skill, now that the skill is learnable at level 5 the proper level requirements have been instated.

Gargoyle's Bite: Level 18
Pearl-encrusted Spear: Level 16
Impaling Harpoon: Level 17
 - **1.15.0:** Also added new low level polearms to existing loottables:
[Rusty Spear](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=80814)
[Piercing Spear](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=80813)
[Satyr Poker](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=80705)
[Energized Spear](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=80811)

author: Xudo
subject: Re: Introduction and Fundamentals
content_md:
> **Daaki wrote: Wed Jul 12, 2023 2:44 pm**
> What does that code represent? I only know a little bit of visual basic, so that's pretty much all Greek to me. But I noticed it's pretty much exactly the same for dodge chance and block chance.
>
>  I'm assuming pvictim is the parry victim, but what variable is GetLevel and whats the 10 and 10.0 beside it mean? On initial glance, it sounded more like the chance is based on the level of the player and the mob, rather than anything to do with weapon skill? Which I guess makes sense given that it's lvl 63 mobs that have 14% chance to parry, but I even if that assumption is right I don't get why block and dodge would have pretty much the same code, as block for example remains 5% with both lvl 60 and 63 mobs. So yeah, I unfortunately don't understand it.
>
>  Does the code actually imply that weapon skill should reduce parry and block chance? What part of the if statement actually does that and how would we know by how much it's meant to reduce the chances by per weapon skill level?

Thats good questions. I'll try to answer them.
> What does that code represent?
Function RollMeleeOutcomeAgainst decides what will be result of attack of "this" unit against "pVictim" of attack.
It is used for any situation. I mean player vs player, player vs mob, mob vs player, mob vs mob.
Result of attack is one of the: miss, dodge, parry, glancing, block, crit, crushing, hit.

I assume you interested in situation when player attacks mob from the front because mobs doesn't parry from behind.
Your specific mob also have nothing to increase dodge, parry or blocks. I will check all kinds of level difference and weapon skill bonuses of player.

Default value for dodge can be found at line [https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L2591](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Unit.cpp#L2591)
next line adds bonuses from equipment talents and skills. So I assume base chance to dodge of mob is 5.00%
Chance to parry can be found here [https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L2623](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Unit.cpp#L2623)
Base chance to parry of mob is 5.00
Chance to block can be found here
[https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L2653](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Unit.cpp#L2653)
Base chance to block of mob is 5.00

To simplify calculations, number 5.00 is converted to 500.

First line mentioning skills is [https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L2115](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Unit.cpp#L2115)
It calls GetSkillMaxForLevel. It is implemented here [https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... ter.h#L328](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/SpellCaster.h#L328)
It figures out level of attacker against current target and multiplies it by 5. It has complex logic when attacker is worldboss, but when attacker is player it just returns player level.

So if you are lvl 60 and attack normal mob of lvl 60, then
attackerMaxSkillValueForLevel = 60*5=300
victimMaxSkillValueForLevel = 60*5=300
here race and bonuses are irrelevant

If you are lvl 60 and attack worldboss, then
attackerMaxSkillValueForLevel = 60*5=300
victimMaxSkillValueForLevel = 63*5=315

After this, server takes into account weapon and defense skills [https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L2118](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Unit.cpp#L2118)
Checks current weapon, checks current player skill for this weapon. For example when you leveled your skill to 80 out of 100.
Logic is in function [https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L6119](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Player.cpp#L6119)
Here you get permanent bonuses and temporary bonuses. I know that talents like Anticipation and racials like Axe Specialization works different than bonuses from Edgemaster's Handguards. But I don't know which are temporary and which are permanent.
Anyway, they sumed both.

So if you are orc with axe of lvl 60, leveled axe skill to 305 then
attackerWeaponSkill = 305
if you are orc with sword of lvl 60, leveled sword skill to 300 then
attackerWeaponSkill = 300
if you are orc with axe of lvl 60, leveled axe skill only to 280 then
attackerWeaponSkill = 280
if you are orc with axe of lvl 60, leveled axe skill only to 305 and wear Edgemaster's Hadguards then
attackerWeaponSkill = 312

Defense skill of mob depends of type and level. But we probably interested in two situations.
[https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L2119](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Unit.cpp#L2119)
If you attack normal mob of 60 lvl
victimDefenseSkill = 300
If you attack worldboss
victimDefenseSkill = 315

After this, server calculates skillDiff [https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L2122](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Unit.cpp#L2122)
skillDiff = attackerWeaponSkill - victimMaxSkillValueForLevel
 60 orc with axe with edgemaster against worldboss
skillDiff = 312-315 = -3
 60 orc with sword against worldboss
skillDiff = 300-315 = -15

Then server finds minimum between attackerMaxSkillValueForLevel and attackerWeaponSkill
[https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L2123](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Unit.cpp#L2123)
and substracts from this value victimMaxSkillValueForLevel
 60 orc with axe with edgemaster against worldboss
cappedSkillDiff = min(300, 312)-315 = 300-315 = -15
 60 orc with sword against worldboss
cappedSkillDiff = min(300, 300)-315 = 300-315 = -15

Then server calculates bonus to block
expression "something ? one : another" means "if something then one else another"
blockSkillBonus = if (pVictim->IsPlayer()){4 * skillDiff } else { 10 * skillDiff}
victim in all our situations is not player

 60 orc with axe with edgemaster against worldboss
blockSkillBonus = 10 * skillDiff = 10 * -3 = -30
 60 orc with sword against worldboss
blockSkillBonus = 10 * skillDiff = 10 * -15 = -150

same for dodge

 60 orc with axe with edgemaster against worldboss
dodgeSkillBonus = 10 * skillDiff = 10 * -3 = -30
 60 orc with sword against worldboss
dodgeSkillBonus = 10 * skillDiff = 10 * -15 = -150

parry expression is pretty sophisticated
[https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L2126](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Unit.cpp#L2126)
int32    parrySkillBonus = pVictim->IsPlayer() ? 4 * skillDiff : cappedSkillDiff < -10 ? 60 * cappedSkillDiff : 20 * cappedSkillDiff;

I assume it means
if (pVictim->IsPlayer()) {
parrySkillBonus = 4 * skillDiff
} else {
if (cappedSkillDiff < -10) {
parrySkillBonus = 60 * cappedSkillDiff
} else {
parrySkillBonus = 20 * cappedSkillDiff
}
}
pVictim is not a player

 60 orc with axe with edgemaster against worldboss. cappedSkillDiff = -15
parrySkillBonus = 60 * -15 = -900
 60 orc with sword against worldboss. cappedSkillDiff = -15
parrySkillBonus = 60 * -15 = -900

Then server rolls one random number from 0 to 9999 (from 0% to 99.99%)
[https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L2128](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Unit.cpp#L2128)
Let it be 7130

then server compares "roll" to miss chance.
 7130 is more than 650, outcome is not miss

then server checks for crit against sitting. not our situation. skip it

dodge chance is reduced by dodgeSkillBonus.
[https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L2158](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Unit.cpp#L2158)

 60 orc with axe with edgemaster against worldboss
dodgeChance = dodgeChance - dodgeSkillBonus = 500 - (-30) = 530
 60 orc with sword against worldboss
dodgeChance = 500 - (-150) = 650 it means 6.5% to dodge

then server compares "roll" to sum of dodge chance + miss chance.
[https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L2165](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Unit.cpp#L2165)
if victim is NPC below level 10, then dodge chance multiplied by (lvl / 10). When level is 1, then 5.0 * 1/10. When level 9 then 5.0 / 9/10.
Not our case with worldboss anyway.

 7130 is more than 500+650, outcome is not dodge

parryChance of mob is reduced by skill bonus
[https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/de ... .cpp#L2178](https://github.com/vmangos/core/blob/development/src/game/Objects/Unit.cpp#L2178)

 60 orc with axe with edgemaster against worldboss
parryChance = parryChance - parrySkillBonus = 500 - (-900) = 1400
 60 orc with sword against worldboss
parryChance = parryChance - parrySkillBonus = 500 - (-900) = 1400 it means 14% to parry
actual skill doesn't seem to do anything

then server compares roll to parry chance
 7130 is more than (500+650+1400), outcome is not parry

I will make github issue to this. Weapon skill actually don't seem to affect parry chance of mob, but it clearly should.
Line "int32    parrySkillBonus = pVictim->IsPlayer() ? 4 * skillDiff : cappedSkillDiff < -10 ? 60 * cappedSkillDiff : 20 * cappedSkillDiff;" probably contain logic error.

author: Xudo
subject: Re: Introduction and Fundamentals
content_md:
I found that current parry formula was made 4 years ago with intention to scale parry chance with weapon skill, but it actually don't scale.
<https://github.com/lh-server/core/pull/236>
So I made a pull request to vMangos with change to make parry actually scale.
<https://github.com/vmangos/core/pull/2075>

I asume main problem is that there is no good data on how parry scales with skill.
Turns out that orc and human tanks will be prefered because they get -9% chance to attack to get parried.
It is more dps and less "parry retaliation".

No significant change for DPS though. They should attack from behind anyway. Mobs don't parry from behind.

author: Dragunovi
subject: Pre-1.17.0 Endgame Item Changes
content_md:
Greetings! We have compiled a list of end-game itemization changes that have been done before the release of Patch 1.17.0: Beyond the Greymane Wall. Please refer to patch specific itemization changelogs for more recent changes and additions. This list primarily concerns items that already exist in vanilla. Any changes not found here like set bonus changes can be found in their respective topic posts.
This list will be primarily split into **two** major sections: **General, Raid Drops**, where the latter is also split into which changes done for which raids.

General:
- Eye of the Beast and Don Rodrigo's Band: Now usable by Shamans.

- Lei of the Lifegiver [+53 Healing Power, +3 MP5] -> [+9 Spirit, +40 Healing Power, +5 MP5]

- Elemental Focus Band: Increased Spellpower from 22 to 24.

- Earthern Guard: Armor buffed from 2468 to 2575, Block buffed from 44 to 47, added 1% Block.

- Windshear Cape: Increased Strength from 8 to 10, added 1% Haste.

- Gauntlets of the Shining Light: Removed 10 Spirit, 22 Healing Power -> 16 Spell Damage

- Death Knight Sabatons: 9 Spirit -> Agility

- Bloodmail Hauberks: 10 Spirit -> Agility

- Handcrafted Mastersmith Leggings: 12 Stamina -> 29 Stamina, 29 Strength -> 12 Strength

- Gift of the Elven Magi: 6 Spirit -> 8 Spell Damage

- Bludstone Hammer: 12 Spirit -> 12 Intellect

- Energized Chestplate: 13 Strength -> 8 Defense

- Backusarian Gauntlets: 9 Strength -> 14 Block Value

- Morlune's Bracers: 7 Stamina -> 12 Stamina, 12 Intellect -> 7 Intellect, 11 Spirit -> 14 Block Value

- Bile-etched Spaulders: 6 Stamina -> 17 Stamina, 17 Strength -> 6 Strength

- Grand Crusader's Helm: 12 Spirit -> 12 Intellect

- Righteous Orb: Critical chance increase has been increased from 3% to 5%.

- Grimy Metal Boots: 17 Strength -> 17 Stamina

- Wind Dancer Boots: 16 Spirit -> 16 Agility, 9 Intellect -> 9 Stamina

Raid Drops:
Zul'Gurub:
- Seafury Leggings: 14 Spirit -> 6 MP5

Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj:
- Boots of the Desert Protector: 14 Stamina -> 20 Stamina, Removed 4 MP5 and 12 Strength, Added %1 Block Chance and 14 Block Value

Molten Core:
- Added six [New](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=81260) [Molten](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=81261) [Core](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=81262) [Trash](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=81263) [Mob](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=81264) [Drops](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=81265)

- Increased the proc chance of Shadowstrike and Thunderstrike from 1 proc per minute to 1.5 procs per minute.

- Increased Health Regen of Sash of Whispered Secrets from 6 to 10 every 5 seconds.

- Removed 11 Spirit from Seal of the Archmagus and added 13 Spellpower instead.

- Removed 10 Spirit from Band of Sulfuras and added 12 Spellpower instead.

- Added 69 Holy Spellpower to Benediction.

Onyxia's Lair
- Removed Spirit from Dragonslayer's Signet, reduced Intellect and Stamina from 12 to 8, and added 18 Spellpower.

- Reduced all resistances of Ring of Binding from 10 to 5, Increased Defense from 4 to 6, Increased Armor from 60 to 100, and added 16 Stamina.

Blackwing Lair:
- Increased the fire delay of Dragonbreath Hand Cannon from 2.6 seconds to 3.1 seconds, the DPS remains the same.

- Added 5% Mana regeneration in combat to Gloves of Rapid Evolution.

- Helm of Endless Rage: [+26 Strength, +26 Agility, +29 Stamina] -> [+25 Strength, +25 Agility, +26 Stamina, +1% Hit]

- Legguards of the Fallen Crusader: [+28 Strength, +22 Agility, +17 Intellect, +22 Stamina] -> [+35 Strength, +20 Agility, +18 Stamina, +1% Hit]

- Removed 17 Spirit from Black Ash Robe and added 20 Spellpower instead.

- Replaced 17 Spirit of Herald of Woe with Agility.

- Replaced 15 Spirit of Primalist's Linked Waistguard with 15 Agility, also added 1% Haste.

- Removed spirit from Girdle of the Fallen Crusader, increased Agility from 10 to 16 and Stamina from 15 to 17. Also added 1% Haste.

- Removed spirit from Primalist's Linked Legguards and added 13 Spellpower instead, also increased Stamina and Intellect from 22 to 23.

- Removed spirit from Angelista's Grasp and added 11 Spellpower instead.

- Removed spirit from Therazane's Link and increased Intellect from 12 to 14, increased Stamina from 22 to 24 and added 1% Haste.

Temple of Ahn'Qiraj:
- Added two new items to Ouro's loot table: <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=21613> | <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=21612>

- Reduced Stamina of Gloves of the Redeemed Prophecy from 20 to 16 and Intellect from 20 to 10, added 12 Agility and replaced 37 Healing Power with 20 Spellpower

- Reduced intellect of Gloves of the Fallen Prophet from 20 to 15, replaced 44 Healing Power with 23 Spellpower. Gloves of the Fallen Prophet have been added to the same trash loot tables as the Gloves of the Redeemed Prophecy as the shaman counterpart of their Prophecy set.

- Increased Spellpower of Scaled Leggings of Qiraji Fury from 36 to 39.

- Replaced 10 Spirit of Gauntlets of the Righteous Champion with Agility.

- Replaced 10 Spirit of Gauntlets of Kalimdor with Agility.

- Replaced 1% Parry on Thick Qirajihide Belt with 1% Dodge, Increased Strength from 10 to 13 and Agility from 15 to 18.

- Increased the fire delay of Blessed Qiraji Musket from 2.6 seconds to 3.1 seconds, the DPS remains the same.

- Swapped around the stats of Mantle of the Desert Crusade and renamed to Mantle of the Redeemed Prophecy: Intellect: 20 to 6 | Stamina: 17 to 20 | Strength: 10 to 17 | Agility: 6 to 10 | Swapped 44 Healing Power for 23 Spellpower and 21 Healing Power

- Reduced Intellect of Mantle of the Desert's Fury from 20 to 15, Increased Strength from 6 to 9, and added 9 Agility. Renamed to Mantle of the Fallen Prophet and got a new model.

Naxxramas:
- Digested Hand of Power: Reduced Intellect from 14 to 8, Reduced Stamina from 10 to 6, Increased MP5 from 10 to 12.

- Pendant of Forgotten Names: Reduced Intellect and Spirit from 16 to 13, Increased MP5 from 7 to 10.

subject: Re: Endgame Item Changes
content_md:
> **Dragunovi wrote: Tue Jul 11, 2023 12:38 pm**
> The origin of the rewards haven't been changed

Perhaps I was not clear.

You are taking a PvP reward and turning it into something that is more suitable for PvE.
PvE players don't want to PvP. They just want their items. They are being a burden to the team and themselves. And you actively encourage them to do that with these changes.

PvP rewards should be bad for PvE (well, not too bad per se, just worse than their PvE loot alternatives acquired with similar effort). And vice versa. PvP rewards should be better for PvP.
MP5 and spirit are not PvP stats. You took a PvP reward and made it more desirable for PvE players.

And this applies to every single PvP reward, not just this one. The changes should be such that PvE players do not want to spend time getting them in the first place, and PvP players do want to spend time getting them.

New Item Sets and Additions to Old Sets:

- New Dragonscale Leatherworking mail healer set: Red Dragon Mail
This set consists of the breastplate already available in Vanilla, boots, leggings and shoulders. Acquired via various recipes around the world.

(3) Set: +26 Healing Power
(4) Set: Your direct healing spells have a chance to place a heal over time on your target, healing 240 over 12 sec.

author: Samsara
subject: Re: Profession Changes and Additons
content_md:
Looking forward to this. A few changes I would like to see that didn't make it:

 - Ability to stack armor kits with enchantments

 - 4 extra slots profession bags as very rare recipes (ie: 0.5% drop rate from world elites and/or 0.05% from normal mobs), not only end game but throughout leveling for each tier of bag progression. In turn you could limit equipping bags with level requirement, so you can't equip best bags on lvl1 toon unless you buy in shop.
It would create a whole incentive to farm these rare recipes and craft them for AH so that twinks and leveling chars can buy better bags at a premium. I know a few people complain about the size of quivers and ammo pouches for instance, but even bags for like enchanting, herbalism, ores, etc could all have those rare recipe upgraded versions.
It would create nice depth of alternate playstyle for people who farm professions to then sell rare stuff at the AH that are in high demand.

Getting a minor amount of XP when leveling professions. Not enough for it to become meta, but enough so that people who love to level them don't feel like it is as much a waste of time to focus on them before reaching max level. For instance leveling 25 levels of a profession should grant you around 2 bubbles of XP bar, relative to your current level, but capped by profession level too (so that you don't gain a full 2 bubbles at lvl59 by leveling profession at Apprentice level.
The caps could work as such:
Apprentice: Full XP gain until level 15, 75% XP gain from 15-30, 50% XP gain from 30-45, 25% XP gain from 45-59
Journeyman: Full XP gain until level 30, 75% XP gain from 30-45, 50% XP gain from 45-59
Expert: Full XP gain until level 45, 75% XP gain from 45-59
Artisan: Always full XP gain

author: Elesion
subject: Re: Profession Changes and Additons
content_md:
> **Diorum1 wrote: Tue Jul 11, 2023 11:54 am**
> > **Dragunovi wrote: Mon Jul 10, 2023 2:28 pm**
> > You can also now acquire the pattern for crafting Enchanted Armor Kits from Lower Karazhan Halls, which grants +8 Intellect and +6 Spellpower instead of the usual defensive values.
>
>   I'm not super familiar with the custom enchants on the server but base classic hands feet and chest are pretty lackluster for casters, +8 int and +6 SP on each of those seem like very good options.
>
>  Could be nice to see specialization armor kits down the line.

Good catch, I didn't even think about Enchanted Armor Kits going into slots other than legs (since they seem so similar to Arcanums). Let's look at the feet/hand/chest slot as well:
This would easily be the best caster boot enchant, except pretty much everyone at high levels wants movement speed on their boots (which is very cheap on top). Not sure how much play the kit will see in this slot. It would be interesting to see devs tackle the movement speed problem, because right now boots are essentially a dead enchanting slot.
Gloves have much more powerful caster enchants, but this will probably be a good mid-range alternative if you don't want to blow >70g on a glove enchant for the AQ20 stuff. Which brings up a good question - what is going to be the price on these, what will the ingredients be looking like? If they're balanced around the leg slot - Arcanum of Focus costs 25g in materials and requires BoP materials from Scholo and some legwork, and the Enchanted Armor Kit is much more powerful. If they're balanced around gloves, the Enchanted Armor Kit will be much weaker than AQ20 enchants. So around 35-40g might be a decent price? Not really entry-level stuff and at that point you might as well save up for an AQ20 enchant for your gloves (though the kit would be general purpose and not limited to 1 school).
Chest is probably the most interesting. Right now +100 mana is the cheaper endgame enchantment for casters (around 15g in materials). And the expensive variant is Greater Stats (stats +4 for around 75g in materials plus a hefty tip because the Formula costs about 1000g). And the changelog mentions that there will be a new "Formula: Enchant Chest - Mighty Mana (+150 Mana)" which is probably more attractive than +4 stats? No idea about the price point for that. The proposed Enchanted Armor Kit would beat all three. It gives 120 mana, 0.13% spell crit from int, 6 spell power - this is *much* better than anything currently available and still better than +150 mana. Which also calls pricing into question yet again... if kits get priced relative to Greater Stats they won't be attractive for any slot other than chest and only for hardcore raiders, but they will be BiS here at least.

Will be interesting to see how this shakes out in practice, especially what the ingredients will be.

On a sidenote: I do hope the dev post has inaccurate wording and "+6 Spellpower" means +damage/healing and not just +damage (although "spell power" on enchants usually refers [only](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=18259) to [damage](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60966)). Would be sad to see healers get shafted out of a great enchant and just see benefit from the 8 int making the boring +150 mana the better choice. (although ideally there'd be a separate healer armor kit because +d/h is a bad use of item budget for healers anyway)

author: Elesion
subject: Re: Profession Changes and Additons
content_md:
> **Samsara wrote: Tue Jul 11, 2023 11:49 am**
> The main issue I have with armor kits is that, they are mainly just good because they're cheap. They are good for leveling, they aren't good for making money. You can farm a lot more leather in minutes than you can sell armor kits at the AH. In contrast, leveling enchanting is very hard work and people will pay a premium for it. LW is poor man's gear buff, and even if it is competitive for a couple classes, it really isn't something worth making a business over. And it's hard enough already to find people to buy LW gear. Skinning is one of my favorite methods for farming mats and making gold, but in current situation it's only good for selling the leather to noobs who want to level their LW, it's not really that good for selling items you actually craft with LW. At least if it stacked with enchants, there would be a much larger demand for them.

So it seems to me you don't actually care about armor kits stacking, you just want *some* kind of way to make a stable profit with LW? Skinning is an incredibly popular choice, because like you say it's just good money without any competition if you skin stuff you're already killing (even more profit if you can farm specialty leathers) and that floods the market with leather. Most professions have the same issue - some ingredients are worthless because they are too numerous, other ingredients are very valuable, but the crafts are usually not. It's the same with Alchemy, Enchanting, Tailoring, Blacksmithing - you craft with ingredients worth 50-600g and get 2-20g in crafting tip/fee/profit margin. LW at least has the best/most profitable cooldown of all crafting professions.

How about a more creative solution than stacking armor kits with enchants? One that tackles multiple problems at a time. Introduce [Dense Leather] as a new tier. It doesn't drop, it has to be crafted and 1 [Dense Leather] is made from 10 [Rugged Leather] (providing a sink for leather, increasing its value). 8 [Dense Leather] create a [Dense Sole], an item that applies to boots, stacks with enchants and provides minor run speed increase (not stacking with any other run speed effects). Only LWs can use [Dense Sole], giving them a service to sell similar to spurs/shield spikes that require Blacksmiths. There will be huge demand, as almost everyone wants increased run speed and it boosts your power by letting you add a regular enchantment to your boots (which also benefits enchanters).
Numbers subject to change and I fully acknowledge that it has an aspect of power creep. It would also invalidate the unqiue effect from [AB reputation boots](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?spell=23990) or the [Centaur Trinket](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60860). But something needs to be done about Enchant Boots - Minor Speed being the only viable boot enchant. I'm not sure the devs fully realize the problem either, since they plan to add enchants like
> **Dragunovi wrote: Mon Jul 10, 2023 2:28 pm**
> - **Enchanting:**
>     - **1.16.6:** Formula: Enchant Boots - Superior Stamina (+14 Stamina)
>
>     - **1.16.6:** Formula: Enchant Boots - Greater Spirit (+12 Spirit)

There are very few applications for these, if any, given they are probably super expensive (so only for raiders and PvP twinks). You can compensate for Stamina in a number of ways (other gear, other enchants, consumables, buffs, more mitigation, better healers), same with Spirit (other gear, other enchants, consumables, mana regen from other classes, buffs, etc). But Enchant Boots - Minor Speed is a totally unique effect that provides make-or-break advantages you cannot get in any other way - getting out of instant-kill zones or other aoe, getting into position faster and thus dealing more dps/heals, catching mobs as a tank earlier, running down other people in PvP, etc. I've been enchanting more Minor Speed even on lvl 19 twinks than Greater Stamina (+7) and that's in a bracket where Stamina is most powerful.

I'm sure there's other ways to tackle the problem, but that is one that came to me because you seem unhappy with LW.

author: Dragunovi
subject: New World Epics and Adjustments
content_md:
Greetings! We have compiled a list of all changes and additions related to epics that are acquired as very rare world drops. This post will be split into two, showcasing the new additions to the roster and then a comprehensive list of changes that have been done to existing world epics.
Profession changes and additions, new relics, endgame itemization, item sets and new item drops are listed on different topics found on the Itemization section.

 **Keep in mind that the changes slated to release in 1.17.0 are subject to change and not final.**

 **New World Epics:**

- [Shieldbreaker Arbalest](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60782)

- [Orb of Purified Light](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60783)

- [Breastplate of Beast Mastery](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60784)

- Effect is being revamped to the following and will be contained in one spell in 1.17.0: Increases your pet's damage by 3%, maximum health by 5% and critical strike chance by 2%.

- [Choker of Cauterization](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60785)

- [The Night Watchman](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60786)

- [Scythe of the Harvest](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60787)

- [Sandals of Inner Peace](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60788)

- [Finkle's Accelerator](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60789)

- [The Wolf Horn of Orgrimmar](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=80793)
 **World Epic Adjustments:**
- Icemail Jerkin: New Effect:
When struck in combat has a chance of freezing the attacker in place for 3 sec.

- Stonerender Gauntlets: New Effect:
Decreases the magical resistances of your spell targets by 10.

- Ring of Saviors: On Use Effect cooldown reduced from 30 to 5 Minutes.

- Lifestone: On Use Effect cooldown reduced from 30 to 15 Minutes. 10 HP5 -> 15 HP5

- Lady Maye's Pendant: 10 Stamina -> 29 Healing Power, 19 Intellect -> 14 Intellect + 2 MP5

- Jeweled Amulet of Cainwyn: 10 Spirit -> 11 Spellpower

- Blade of Hanna: All Stats increased from 11 to 14, Added +1% Hit and Crit

- **1.17.0:** Cloudkeeper Legplates: On Use Attack Power cooldown reduced from 15 to 10 minutes.

- **1.17.0:** Lion Horn of Stormwind: Proc changed from: "When struck in combat has a 1% chance of increasing all party member's armor by 250 for 30 sec." to "When struck in combat has a 2% chance of increasing all party member's attack and casting speed by 5% for 30 sec."

author: Dragunovi
subject: List of New Relics
content_md:
Greetings! We have compiled a list of all new relic additions for our hybrid friends to use. Our vision on relics is that relics should add new effects or change abilities in a substantial way and not to function as flat power upgrades for specific abilities like later expansions did. Though you might also encounter backports of some relic effects from later expansions and return of some retired effects from earlier versions of Vanilla.
The list will be consist of three sections, one for each hybrid class: Shaman, Paladin and Druid.

 **Keep in mind that the relics slated to be added are subject to change and not final.**

Shaman:
 **Updated in 1.17.1:** Totem of the Endless Flicker - Drops from Witch Doctor Zum'rah in Zul'Farrak.
Effect: Increases the duration of your Flame Shock by 3 secs.

 **1.16.1:** Totem of Earthstorm - Drops from Dark Reaver of Karazhan outside Karazhan.
Effect: +5 to Strength of Earth and Grace of Air totem effect.

 **1.17.0:** Totem of the Stonebreaker - Drops from Solnius in the Emerald Sanctum.
Effect: Your Shock spells have a chance to grant 100 Attack Power for 10 sec.

 **1.17.0:** Totem of Crackling Thunder - Drops from Grizikil in Lower Karazhan Halls.
Effect: Your Stormstrike and Lightning Bolt have a chance to also grant 15% attack and casting speed for 8 sec.

 **1.17.0:** Totem of Bad Mojo - Drops from Shadeflayer Goliath in Hyjal.
Effect: Your Hex lasts 1.5 secs longer.

 **Updated in 1.17.1:** Totem of the Calming River - Drops from Epidamu in Caverns of Time: The Black Morass.
Effect: Your Water Shield ability grants an additional 8 mana per 5 sec. while active. In addition the amount of mana restored by your Water Shield when attacked is increased by 10.

 **1.17.2:** Totem of Static Charge - Drops from Zandara Windhoof in the Wailing Caverns.
Effect: Your Lightning Bolt has a 10% chance to shock your enemy, dealing 30-50 Nature damage. This effect generates no threat.

 **1.17.2:** Totem of Broken Earth - Drops from Rupturan the Broken in Upper Karazhan.
Effect: Increases damage done by Earth Shock by up to 100. Earth Shock now slows attack speed by 15% for 8 sec.

Vanilla Totem Changes:
- **1.17.1:** Totem of Flowing Water: Now grants up to 25 mana per Lesser Healing Wave cast up from 10.
Paladin:
 **1.16.?:** Libram of Veracity - Drops from Dark Reaver of Karazhan outside Karazhan.
Effect: Reduces the casting cost of all your Blessings by 15.

 **1.16.?:** Libram of the Resolute - Drops from Scarlet Commander Mograine in Scarlet Monastery: Cathedral.
Effect: Increases the duration of your Blessing of Freedom by 1 sec.

 **1.17.0:** Libram of the Dreamguard - Drops from Solnius in the Emerald Sanctum.
Effect: Increase the number of charges of your Holy Shield by 1.

 **1.17.0:** Libram of the Justicar - Drops rarely from trash mobs in Gilneas City.
Effect: Reduces the cooldown of Hammer of Justice by 5 secs.

 **1.17.0:** Libram of the Faithful - Drops from Lord Blackwald II in Lower Karazhan Halls.
Effect: Your Consecration reduces damage taken by 5% for party members that are inside it.

 **1.17.2:** Libram of Radiance - Drops from Brother Wystan in Scarlet Monastery: Library.
Effect: Increases your chance to critically strike with Holy Light and Holy Strike by 1%.

 **1.17.2:** Libram of the Eternal Tower - Drops from Echo of Medivh in Upper Karazhan.
Effect: Reduces the cooldown of your Holy Strike and Crusader Strike by 0.5 sec.

Vanilla Libram Changes:
- **1.17.0:** Libram of Fervor: Holy Spellpower increase is now 7 per stack of Crusader Strike, stacking to 35 extra Holy Spellpower with five stacks of Crusader Strike. The original version of the relic increased the holy spellpower component of the Judgement of the Crusader debuff by 33, which this value was unintentionally left the same when the source of the holy spellpower was shifted to Crusader Strike, allowing this effect to stack up to 5 times, resulting in a crazy **165** holy spellpower, this change corrects it to the original intended power of the relic, with 2 extra holy spellpower.

- **1.17.1:** Libram of Truth: Devotion Aura reduces physical damage taken by 2% instead of granting 55 extra armor.
Druid:
 **Updated in 1.17.1:** Idol of Evergrowth - Drops from Razorlash in Maraudon.
Effect: Your Thorns additionally gives a 3% chance when attacked to inflict 15-20 Nature damage to nearby enemies.

 **1.16.?:** Idol of the Wildshifter -  Drops from Dark Reaver of Karazhan outside Karazhan.
Effect: Reduces the Mana cost of your shapeshifting spells by 75.

 **1.17.0:** Idol of the Emerald Rot - Drops from Solnius in the Emerald Sanctum.
Effect: Your finishing moves have a 20% chance per combo point to deal 150 - 191 Nature damage.

 **1.17.0:** Idol of the Moonfang - Drops from Clawlord Howlfang in Lower Karazhan Halls.
Effect: Increases the critical chance provided by Leader of the Pack and Moonkin Aura by 1%.

 **1.17.0:** Idol of Savagery - Drops from Rotmaw in Caverns of Time: The Black Morass.
Effect: Reduces the time between periodic ticks and duration of Rake and Rip by 10%.

 **1.17.2:** Idol of the Apex Predator - Drops from Vangros in the Wailing Caverns.
Effect: Reduces the Rage cost of your Demoralizing Roar by 2.

 **1.17.2:** Idol of Laceration - Drops from Keeper Gnarlmoon in Upper Karazhan.
Effect: Your Rip has a 20% chance per combo point to make your next Shred refund 15 Energy.

 **1.17.2:** Idol of Ebb and Flow - Drops from Cla'ckora (Summoned World Boss)
Effect: Reduce the cast time of Starfire by 0.2 seconds.

content_md:
> **Dragunovi wrote: Mon Jul 10, 2023 2:30 pm**
> **1.16.6:** Libram of the Faithful - Drops from Lord Blackwald II in Lower Karazhan Halls.
>  Effect: Your Consecration reduces damage taken by 5% for party members that are inside it.

Please don't try to fix class balance problems with max level equipment.

Paladin's issue is that it lacks the defenses that Warrior and Druid have. Paladin doesn't have the baseline -10% damage taken of Defensive Stance, nor do they have the massive armor bonus that Bear Form has. Tacking 5% DR onto Consecration is not only awkward but it means you only get that much-needed DR once you're max level and get geared enough for that dungeon and get the item to drop.....and only when Consecrate is down.

Why not attach that DR% onto Holy Shield instead? Or even make it part of Ardent Defender?

Holy Shield (Rank 1) - Now also reduces damage taken by 3% while active.
Holy Shield (Rank 2) - Now also reduces damage taken by 6% while active.
Holy Shield (Rank 3) - Now also reduces damage taken by 9% while active.

Easy enough. Or for Ardent Defender:

 -When you have less than 35% health, all damage taken is reduced by 25%. Also reduces damage taken by 10% while Holy Shield is active.

We need to be fixing class balance problems at the spell/talent level, not band-aid fixes with pieces of gear.

content_md:
> **Tenant wrote: Tue Jul 11, 2023 3:11 am**
> You know what, don't bother. [...]
>  Better no changes than filler changes.

That was my knee-jerk reaction as well. They seemed utterly underwhelming at first glance. But maybe we should take a closer look?

> **Tenant wrote: Tue Jul 11, 2023 3:11 am**
> Brutality and Ferocity beat every one of these except the Wildshifter, and Wildshiter was a mistake to begin with.

I think everyone with half a brain has to agree that Ferocity and Brutality are incredibly overpowered for how early you can get them. They had to be nerfed in TBC because they were BiS forever, no contest. Lowering an otherwise flat cost is just a super powerful effect. I think it's arguable that Brutality and Ferocity were a mistake. Don't get me wrong, they're fun and I love them, but relics were supposed to have quirky and situational effects to boost the hybrid classes. This is just a flat power increase with perfect scaling that you get very early on.
But maybe we're underrating the new idols? You mention Wildshifter and when I first joined TWoW and looked at the database I thought Wildshifter was a joke item. I couldn't imagine a use for it. But there's the very narrow niche of powershifting where it shines.

> **Dragunovi wrote: Mon Jul 10, 2023 2:30 pm**
> [Idol of Evergrowth](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=51802) - Drops from Razorlash in Maraudon: Orange.
>  The effect is slated to change in 1.16.6 to the following: Increases the duration of Barkskin by 2 sec.

You can get this super early and the old effect (increases the duration of Thorns) was exclusively one of utility with zero in-combat advantage. Also weirdly close to the T1 set bonus. I saw it drop on my Mara quest run and didn't even roll on it over the other druid because it provided me with no appreciable advantage. So I welcome pretty much any change. Barkskin duration is weird and interesting. It's not super overpowered but it does provide some advantage, potentially a lot more if we ever get to use Barkskin in bear form. I'm fine with this change.

> **Dragunovi wrote: Mon Jul 10, 2023 2:30 pm**
> **1.16.6:** Idol of the Emerald Rot - Drops from Solnius in the Emerald Sanctum.
>  Effect: Your finishing moves have a 20% chance per combo point to deal 90 - 130 Nature damage.

This is like discount rogue instant poison added to cat form? Also one of the very few ways of doing magical damage as a cat. It drops from the endgame raid. So either we get encounters where nature damage is required (like Viscidus requires frost?) or this is just a buff for non-powershifters who right now have no idol at all (Ferocity doesn't affect Shred).

> **Dragunovi wrote: Mon Jul 10, 2023 2:30 pm**
> **1.16.6:** Idol of the Moonfang - Drops from Clawlord Howlfang in Lower Karazhan Halls.
>  Effect: Increases the critical chance provided by Leader of the Pack and Moonkin Aura by 1%.

If you think the new idols are trash, you might be horribly underrating this one. Drops from an entry-raid and might be BiS for any raiding dps spec. Right now moonkins have Idol of the Moon which slightly boosts Moonfire damage. This gives 1% spell crit to 5 casters in your raid - it's a massive massive buff over Idol of the Moon! It's literally half a mage Atiesh! And it might be even better for raiding cat dps, because 1% melee crit automatically means 1% more damage (melee crits are +100% without any talents, unlike spell crits). Again, Ferocity isn't on the table (doesn't affect Shred) so right now you only have Wildshifter (though the power rating after the nerf with the next patch remains to be seen) and maybe you don't want to (or come next patch: don't have to???) powershift?
I think this idol is incredibly powerful and any raid who already has a dps druid will want them to use it.

> **Dragunovi wrote: Mon Jul 10, 2023 2:30 pm**
> **1.16.6:** Idol of Savagery - Drops from Rotmaw in Caverns of Time: The Black Morass.
>  Effect: Reduces the time between periodic ticks and duration of Rake and Rip by 10%.

I don't get it, but maybe I don't understand the mechanics enough. Also drops from a pre-raid dungeon, so it shouldn't be surprising if this isn't super powerful. Increases armor-ignoring DoTs, maybe for PvP burst?

In conclusion: The idols could be better. The one from Emerald Sanctum seems bafflingly weak compared to how late you get it and also weirdly geared for personal dps (so solo play or 5 people groups). While the one from Karazhan Halls seems very overpowered compared to how early you get it and weirdly geared for raids. But otherwise they seem completely fine to me upon closer look. Every non-healing spec gets a boost and I suspect we might be missing mechanical changes that would really make these idols shine (use Barkskin in bear form, viable raid cat dps without powershifting, etc).

content_html:
I think everyone with half a brain has to agree that Ferocity and Brutality are incredibly overpowered for how early you can get them. They had to be nerfed in TBC because they were BiS forever, no contest. Lowering an otherwise flat cost is just a super powerful effect. I think it's arguable that Brutality and Ferocity were a mistake. Don't get me wrong, they're fun and I love them, but relics were supposed to have quirky and situational effects to boost the hybrid classes. This is just a flat power increase with perfect scaling that you get very early on.
Have you seen the relics for other classes?
And I'll take this "nerf" any day.
You can get this super early and the old effect (increases the duration of Thorns) was exclusively one of utility with zero in-combat advantage. Also weirdly close to the T1 set bonus. I saw it drop on my Mara quest run and didn't even roll on it over the other druid because it provided me with no appreciable advantage. So I welcome pretty much any change. Barkskin duration is weird and interesting. It's not super overpowered but it does provide some advantage, potentially a lot more if we ever get to use Barkskin in bear form. I'm fine with this change.
You will get to very strange places discussing what-ifs. I discuss what's offered now.
Barkskin is used essentially never. Its only niche is pvp moonkins, and that slot is occupied with Moon idol.
1.16.6: Idol of the Emerald Rot - Drops from Solnius in the Emerald Sanctum.
Effect: Your finishing moves have a 20% chance per combo point to deal 90 - 130 Nature damage.
This is like discount rogue instant poison added to cat form? Also one of the very few ways of doing magical damage as a cat. It drops from the endgame raid. So either we get encounters where nature damage is required (like Viscidus requires frost?) or this is just a buff for non-powershifters who right now have no idol at all (Ferocity doesn't affect Shred).
Again, "what if we get encounters...". If we get such encounters, you'll be better off just spamming Wrath.
This idol is an attempt to add burst damage to cat, which is desirable in pvp. I commend the attempt, but as is, I'm pretty sure it's not going to be used.
1.16.6: Idol of the Moonfang - Drops from Clawlord Howlfang in Lower Karazhan Halls.
Effect: Increases the critical chance provided by Leader of the Pack and Moonkin Aura by 1%.
If you think the new idols are trash, you might be horribly underrating this one. Drops from an entry-raid and might be BiS for any raiding dps spec. Right now moonkins have Idol of the Moon which slightly boosts Moonfire damage. This gives 1% spell crit to 5 casters in your raid - it's a massive massive buff over Idol of the Moon! It's literally half a mage Atiesh! And it might be even better for raiding cat dps, because 1% melee crit automatically means 1% more damage (melee crits are +100% without any talents, unlike spell crits). Again, Ferocity isn't on the table (doesn't affect Shred) so right now you only have Wildshifter (though the power rating after the nerf with the next patch remains to be seen) and maybe you don't want to (or come next patch: don't have to???) powershift?
I think this idol is incredibly powerful and any raid who already has a dps druid will want them to use it.
Counting like that, Moonkin aura by itself is 1.5 mage Atiesh! Have you seen guild recruitment ads? Are moonkins in high demand?
But I agree, this one actually has its uses.

 **Keep in mind that the changes and additions are subject to change and not final.**

Introducing Two New Stats:
We're adding **two** new stats with the release of 1.17.0, there might not be a lot of items with these stats currently but the amount of them will increase as we introduce more content, they're as follows:
- **Vampirism:** You can find this effect listed as "% of your damage is returned as healing." which is pretty self explanatory, especially useful for outdoor content.

- **Reduced Chance to Get Critically Hit:** Basically what it says in the name, this is primarily a PvP stat with some use to tanks.

- Haste stat now grants **double** casting speed of the attack speed bonus. Ex. Increases your attack speed by 1% and casting speed by 2%.
EDIT: This change had to be reverted last second due to overpowered synergy with healers, more powerful haste might return for casters as a seperate stat at a later patch.

- In addition, Increased Chance to Parry stat cost has been decreased from **15.65 to 13.35.**
This essentially means items with parry now have room for a bit more stats. Parry Haste was valued too much compared to Dodge where the Increased Parry got its extra cost. We hope this makes the stat more viable to use in gearing without sacrificing too many other stats.
This change affects **40+ items**, we won't list all changes here for that reason, but you can expect small increases in other stats the item utilizes.

 **Item Adjustments**
| As a (not so) small note on items such as Bloodvine, Titanic Leggings and Spellweaver's Turban and other similiar items that stick out compared the rest, keep in mind that these items were made as catch-up gear later into the lifecycle of Vanilla with the thought that earlier released raids were being ran much less than before and were made to skip gear progression by a long shot and get into the endgame much faster, but Turtle is different in this regard. All raids are being ran quite often and there's no end to the content development and to the lifecycle of the server of the server.

The existence of catch-up gear in an environment there is no need to catch up causes a lot of issues in the gearing flow the endgame at large, especially the early endgame where this affects the first few raids you conquer. Our intentions aren't to punish players by taking their power away, its to provide a healthy progression of items and for the players to get the enjoyment of acquiring new upgrades to their items at a decent pace and not get stuck with a single piece of item for the entirety of the game.

All of these nerfs were both compensated via the additions of new endgame gear with Lower Karazhan Halls and the Emerald Sanctum and via making already existing items powerful enough to act as a step in gear progression for players to enjoy (which you will see in this list of changes). Thank you for understanding.

content_html:
Greetings! At long last, here is the changelog detailing almost all single item and item related addition and change arrived with the release of Patch 1.17.0: Beyond the Greymane Wall

Keep in mind that the changes and additions are subject to change and not final.


Introducing Two New Stats:
We're adding two new stats with the release of 1.17.0, there might not be a lot of items with these stats currently but the amount of them will increase as we introduce more content, they're as follows:
  • Vampirism: You can find this effect listed as "% of your damage is returned as healing." which is pretty self explanatory, especially useful for outdoor content.
  • Reduced Chance to Get Critically Hit: Basically what it says in the name, this is primarily a PvP stat with some use to tanks.
  • Haste stat now grants double casting speed of the attack speed bonus. Ex. Increases your attack speed by 1% and casting speed by 2%.
    EDIT: This change had to be reverted last second due to overpowered synergy with healers, more powerful haste might return for casters as a seperate stat at a later patch.
  • In addition, Increased Chance to Parry stat cost has been decreased from 15.65 to 13.35.
    This essentially means items with parry now have room for a bit more stats. Parry Haste was valued too much compared to Dodge where the Increased Parry got its extra cost. We hope this makes the stat more viable to use in gearing without sacrificing too many other stats.
    This change affects 40+ items, we won't list all changes here for that reason, but you can expect small increases in other stats the item utilizes.
  • Druids can now wield Polearms! Remember to get your training from your capital city.
  • Polearms below Item Level 25 had their level requirements adjusted to be usable at a lower level:
    • Gargoyle's Bite: Level 18
    • Pearl-encrusted Spear: Level 16
    • Impaling Harpoon: Level 17
    • Also added new gray and green low level polearms to existing loottables:
      Rusty Spear and Piercing Spear [+3 Agility]
  • Most Two-Handed Maces, Polearms and the few physical damage oriented Staves now grant Feral Attack Power, granting 14 for every item level above 60.
    Below are a few examples and not an extensive list of all weapons with Feral AP:
    • Bonecrusher: 42 Feral AP
    • Unyielding Maul: 28 Feral AP
    • Boneshatter Maul: 70 Feral AP
    • Nat Pagle's Fish Terminator: 70 Feral AP
    • Finkle's Lava Dredger: 140 Feral AP
    • Herald of Woe: 210 Feral AP
    • Barb of the Sand Reaver: 238 Feral AP
    • R14 PvP Polearms: 252 Feral AP
    • Eye of Nerub: 322 Feral AP
  • Added new rare trash mob drops to Stormwind Vault, Black Morass and Crescent Grove, with eight of them being added for the first two while adding four to latter due to the fact it already has four drops.
  • Four new items have been added to the Caverns of Time: Black Morass loottables! Idol of Savagery and Wraps of the Transmogrified have been added to Rotmaw while Totem of the Flowing Timeways and Fabric of Time has been added to the new boss Epidamu.
  • Added too many new quest rewards to count. Some notable ares rare quality quest reward items from Gilneas for completing Gilneas City for both factions, a new Gnomeregan quest accessible in the Gnomeregan Reclamation Facility and the end reward trinket for finishing the questline related to the new Chimaera Roost Vale in Southern Feralas to name a few.
Item Adjustments
|
As a (not so) small note on items such as Bloodvine, Titanic Leggings and Spellweaver's Turban and other similiar items that stick out compared the rest, keep in mind that these items were made as catch-up gear later into the lifecycle of Vanilla with the thought that earlier released raids were being ran much less than before and were made to skip gear progression by a long shot and get into the endgame much faster, but Turtle is different in this regard. All raids are being ran quite often and there's no end to the content development and to the lifecycle of the server of the server.

The existence of catch-up gear in an environment there is no need to catch up causes a lot of issues in the gearing flow the endgame at large, especially the early endgame where this affects the first few raids you conquer. Our intentions aren't to punish players by taking their power away, its to provide a healthy progression of items and for the players to get the enjoyment of acquiring new upgrades to their items at a decent pace and not get stuck with a single piece of item for the entirety of the game.

All of these nerfs were both compensated via the additions of new endgame gear with Lower Karazhan Halls and the Emerald Sanctum and via making already existing items powerful enough to act as a step in gear progression for players to enjoy (which you will see in this list of changes). Thank you for understanding.

    Cleaning Cloth (Survival):
    • The outline for the Cleaning Cloth can now be acquired from Nesigwary's Camp and learned if you have 50 Survival. Costing some silk cloth and a volatile rum, this cloth can be applied on any weapon to wipe off any temporary weapon enchants such as sharpening stones, weightstones, poisons and other effects. Especially useful if you get an opportunity to utilize a Windfury Totem which its effects are prevented by your own applied items.

author: Elesion
subject: Re: 1.16.6 Itemization Changelog (Work In Progress)
content_md:
> **Dragunovi wrote: Mon Jul 10, 2023 2:32 pm**
> - Lei of the Lifegiver [+53 Healing Power, +3 MP5] -> [+9 Spirit, +40 Healing Power, +5 MP5]

This is not a massive nerf so I'm not really up in arms about it, but I'm fairly baffled by it for a number of reasons:
 1) Gearing as a healer is hard in the early raids. +heal on weapons wasn't really a thing when MC and BWL were designed. That's why ZG weapons blow MC gear clean out of the water for healers. AQ20 doesn't offer any healing weapons at all. BWL has damage/healing weapons that Spriests and Moonkins can make better use of. And in terms of healer off-hands there's a single one [from ZG](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=19922) geared only towards crit healers. What kind of raid progression is "skipped" using Lei of the Lifegiver? There's nothing there to be skipped. The first healing off-hand that drops from a 40 person raid ([Sartura's Might](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=21666)) is a clear upgrade over Lei. Turtle has added some healer off-hands to worldbosses ([1](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=51778) and [2](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=83480)) but people aren't exactly voluntarily skipping those in troves... Besides 1h+oh is already harder to gear than picking up a 2h. Being able to get decent stuff from vendors makes it way more viable.
 2) Why single out healers? None of the other AV rewards are being nerfed. Don Julio's and Unstoppable Force skip quite a bit of progression too... Besides, there's already barely any rewards for healers in PvP. Lei, the R14 weapons, and the Blood Ring blue ring. That's it, afaik nothing else is geared towards healers.
 3) The catch-up reasoning is hard to understand. With the Silvermoon/Revantusk rewards you can pick up your healing pre-raid BiS 1h+oh the day you hit lvl 60, skipping all dungeon progression. And even the same patch is supposed to buff some crafted gear, so it's more on par with those bad bad late-development-cycle catch-up items (Thorium Brotherhood items buffed "to achieve parity between recipe crafts that was introduced early and late in the lifecycle of Vanilla"). I don't really get it.

> **Dragunovi wrote: Mon Jul 10, 2023 2:32 pm**
> **Naxx Trash Mob Drop Adjustments:**
>  Reduced item level of trash drops from Naxxramas by 5: (83 to 78 for normal, 85 to 80 for class specific pieces) to make more sense with their location of acquisition, currently the trash drop weapons are even better than non-wing end bosses, making them way too powerful while being too easily farmed.
> - Ghoul Skin Tunic: [+411 Armor, +40 Strength, +22 Stamina, +2% Critical Chance] -> [+369 Armor, +34 Strength, +22 Stamina, +2% Critical Chance]

The problem is, the (very sensible) reasoning for toning down the trash drops so people have to gun for boss drops doesn't really apply to this item. There's nothing better for feral druids. This is currently BiS, both for tanking and dps. Feral dps has a minimally-worse side-grade in [Vest of Swift Execution](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=21680) which comes from Bug Trio (so not exactly a super hard fight either and it would top you out even earlier in raid progression) that will now become the new BiS. But tank is in a pretty bad position. The new Ghoul Skin Tunic is probably still BiS over all (with crit for threat generation), but mitigation BiS suddenly comes from [Ebonroc in BWL](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=19405). No armor value upgrade after the first half of BWL and no dps upgrade after the first third of AQ40 is just sad.

> **Dragunovi wrote: Mon Jul 10, 2023 2:32 pm**
> - Most Two-Handed Maces and Polearms now grant Feral Attack Power, granting 14 for every item level above 60.
>    Below are a few examples and not an extensive list of all weapons with Feral AP:
>     - Bonecrusher: 42 Feral AP
>
>     - Unyielding Maul: 28 Feral AP
>
>     - Boneshatter Maul: 70 Feral AP
>
>     - Nat Pagle's Fish Terminator: 70 Feral AP
>
>     - Finkle's Lava Dredger: 140 Feral AP
>
>     - Herald of Woe: 210 Feral AP
>
>     - Barb of the Sand Reaver: 238 Feral AP
>
>     - R14 PvP Polearms: 252 Feral AP
>
>     - Eye of Nerub: 322 Feral AP

Huge! This solves so many problems in one fell swoop - no feral AP outside of raid drops, feral AP only on 1h making 2h not viable, best 2h dropping from BWL since weapon damage (a proxy for ilvl) doesn't matter, R14 weapons being completely unattractive to ferals, etc. It's a bit of a shame that all the cool 1h weapons geared specifically towards ferals will disappear from the ultra-endgame (everyone is going to use a Might of Menethil, probably even tanks, since it's incredibly far ahead of everything else just by virtue of its ilvl). Will be interesting to see in practice, but already looking very neat and also answers the question whether opening up polearms to druids would even be all that useful (I was very skeptical).

> **Dragunovi wrote: Mon Jul 10, 2023 2:32 pm**

> Vampirism: You can find this effect listed as "% of your damage is returned as healing." which is pretty self explanatory, especially useful for outdoor content.

Seems like a stat that should be class specific, i.e. stacking with Vampiric Embrace/Vampiric Touch to give Spriest more utility. In the future I can see Paladins solo AoE farming dungeons especially in ZG, BRD, HFQ, and DME. Moreover mages will now be able to AoE farm with a lot less effort.

Some of these new stats seem more likely to take away the uniqueness of the class played and the role their supposed to fill, slowly progressing towards a all classes can do everything scenario.

> All raids are being ran quite often and there's no end to the content development and to the lifecycle of the server of the server.

> The existence of catch-up gear in an environment there is no need to catch up causes a lot of issues in the gearing flow the endgame at large, especially the early endgame where this affects the first few raids you conquer. author: Jaycegod2
subject: Re: 1.16.6 Itemization Changelog (Work In Progress)
content_md:
Probably a hot take but idc

You're going to ruin PvP if you're not careful with how much reduced % to be crit and "vampirism" you add to the game.

Warhammer Online/Return of Reckoning has similar stats (reduced chance to be crit & life regen). However where they fumbled these stats is the fact that they oversaturated HP regen into way too many & easy access items (trinkets, easy to farm jewels, talent trees etc).

Reduced chance to be crit is a whole other subject as well. Most people from WAR/RoR found it mandatory to stack at least -15% chance to be crit. Which is OK in a game where people are getting up to 30-50% critical hit rating, but in a game like wow vanilla, most people are barely running 20% crit.

If these stats get out of control or are sloppily implemented into too many easy access items, you will further exacerbate balance issues with tank builds in PvP- ultimately frustrating your arguably most loyal category of players.

You will definitely usher in a new meta to stack -15% chance to be crit, heavy health regen/vampirism builds that just never die or seemingly lose enough health for anyone to use a finisher. Believe me when I say I've seen these stats in other MMOs become over saturated and absolutely ruin burst builds in pvp and beckon a deftard/regen build meta, something that I can confidently say, nobody finds fun to play or play against.

If these stats get out of control or are sloppily implemented into too many easy access items, you will further exacerbate balance issues with tank builds in PvP- ultimately frustrating your arguably most loyal category of players.

You will definitely usher in a new meta to stack -15% chance to be crit, heavy health regen/vampirism builds that just never die or seemingly lose enough health for anyone to use a finisher. Believe me when I say I've seen these stats in other MMOs become over saturated and absolutely ruin burst builds in pvp and beckon a deftard/regen build meta, something that I can confidently say, nobody finds fun to play or play against.

author: Elesion
subject: Re: 1.16.6 Itemization Changelog (Work In Progress)
content_md:
> **Nandiebs wrote: Mon Jul 17, 2023 11:20 am**
> First of all, the whole premise that catch up gear on Twow is not needed couldn't be more wrong and I think it shows you are out of touch with the player base.
>  It is a fully progressed server and the massive gear difference leads to very toxic power dynamics in both raids and pvp.
>  By removing these catch up pieces you are essentially telling newer players to fuck off and catering to decked out old-heads.

No, I think that is the point. People look at all the Naxx-clearing guilds and say "I want in on that", skipping all the progression. But the progression is being run, there is no need for this skip. If you join a raid and you're so undergeared that you feel people are toxic towards you, you're in the wrong raid. Simple as that. It's just greed that ends up hurting yourself. Because in 2 months of a massive uphill struggle you will have seen everything and apart from single items you will be fully BiS geared. That's a silly approach to a forever-Vanilla server imo.

I hit 60 in April. Then I ran dungeons for 2 months and got geared. It was a blast and I got to know a lot of people. That made me end up with a lot of guild offers, including several from guilds that have Naxx on farm. I could have had T3 in just a few weeks! You know what I did? I joined a guild that had barely killed Rag and has zero progress in BWL. Because that's the gameplay of WoW. You start at the bottom and work your way up. If you hit 60 and jump into Naxx gear the next week you're skipping most of the endgame and run the risk of horribly burning out in 2 months because there's simply nothing left to do.

Dragunovi is right, there is no *need* to skip progression or catch-up. Plenty of guilds start raiding every month, it's quite easy to find a nice raid group that will take you from dungeon blues to your first raid epics. You might still *want* to skip into T3 because that's just your idea of fun, but I don't think it's an option TWoW as a forever-Vanilla server has to endorse or support.
Now I don't agree with some of the proposed changes for different reasons, but that's another story. Catch-up gear is definitely not super needed on a server that covers all stages of progression very well. None of the raid content on TWoW is "over" and thus meant to be skipped, it's all very active.

I joined a guild that had barely killed Rag and has zero progress in BWL. Because that's the gameplay of WoW. You start at the bottom and work your way up. If you hit 60 and jump into Naxx gear the next week you're skipping most of the endgame and run the risk of horribly burning out in 2 months because there's simply nothing left to do.

Dragunovi is right, there is no *need* to skip progression or catch-up. Plenty of guilds start raiding every month, it's quite easy to find a nice raid group that will take you from dungeon blues to your first raid epics. You might still *want* to skip into T3 because that's just your idea of fun, but I don't think it's an option TWoW as a forever-Vanilla server has to endorse or support.
Now I don't agree with some of the proposed changes for different reasons, but that's another story. Catch-up gear is definitely not super needed on a server that covers all stages of progression very well. None of the raid content on TWoW is "over" and thus meant to be skipped, it's all very active.

Its totally fine to have different gear sources but when the items are designed and itemized to directly cut a part of the game this causes issues for us.

You can very well see this with most if not all item nerfs that have been done: Bloodvine Set was so powerful its the best ever armor Booökins were able to get *and* rivaled **Tier 3** for most caster classes to the point you could make an argument to stick with it forever, Lionheart Helm was also to this point where there wasn't anything able to beat it in terms of power in any point of the game, we've even reduced the nerf on Titanic Leggings because we believe we were too harsh on the nerfs. Naxxramas Trash Drops are one of the biggest culprits, these items were on par and most times even better than actual Naxxramas boss dropped items, and these items being farmable with someone kiting creatures around the main room whether you were a fresh 60 or a hardened veteran is a big issue (which might be adressed by more than nerfs at one point.)

The ability to skip straight to the end of the game with these pieces is not healthy at all for any server that intends to exist for more than a year, Blizzard have went for these changes because by then they already had TBC deep in development and knew none of these items would matter the second it released, but for us its not an option if the level cap is going to be 60 forever.

Do keep in mind that most of these nerfs bring buffs for pieces that were originally designed as an upgrade for those pieces but fell flat due to the poor itemization done to them, which we've tinkered with to serve as a proper upgrade from the items we've altered. Its not about intentionally messing or upsetting people, its our job to ensure the endgame player progression isn't demolished by something that leaps 10 steps ahead of an item you acquire at the same stage of the game, acquiring upgrades is part of the fun after all.

I mostly wanted to see how big of a text box I could accumulate through requotes but also echo this sentiment.

If you're going to nerf these raid catch up items do it more subtely. Slightly reducing Bloodvine/LHH/Titanic DPS output through reducing the pure SP & STR of the items might make some sense but fully reworking them to have stamina changes the purpose of the items and homogenizes the gear available to players. Trust me, no one wants to use these items forever but they do serve an important role in the ecosystem by allowing an early 60 player the ability to get up the crucial hit rating necessary to do end game raiding but at a real cost, their health pool. I see that some of these changes have been slightly altered from the beginning and I believe that's at least a step in the right direction.

In regards to the Naxx trash drops. I think ilvl 80 would be a more appropriate nerf. In the case of the most egregious example, MSA, it would be slightly above R14 and slightly below Naxx boss drops. It's still not a sword so rogues will still seek to get CTS/AQR/R14 but would still leave it in the ranks of what it should be.. a weapon from the hardest content in the game.

I think the changes you make, in general, come off as quite transparently tailored to buff the hybrid classes you play and back hand the more specialized classes that you don't. Where is the ilvl 80 slow 1H sword? This seems like the biggest hole in vanilla itemization, period. A rogue must go from ilvl 77/78 to 89 with 0 opportunities in between.

Astrld, Nachichi, Snapcaster, Rafiq, Tazri

Do keep in mind that most of these nerfs bring buffs for pieces that were originally designed as an upgrade for those pieces but fell flat due to the poor itemization done to them, which we've tinkered with to serve as a proper upgrade from the items we've altered. Its not about intentionally messing or upsetting people, its our job to ensure the endgame player progression isn't demolished by something that leaps 10 steps ahead of an item you acquire at the same stage of the game, acquiring upgrades is part of the fun after all.
Naxx trash weapons serve to patch itemization holes (missing options). HoD is the ONLY Naxx-ilvl fast dagger for rogue off hand/tank main hand. MSA is a good catch up for AQR which has an abysmally low drop rate (rogue issue) and a good protection paladin weapon as well as a staple of rogue PvP (remember that rogues are not good in PvP here so nerfing MSA hurts them further).
By nerfing those weapons you're effectively removing gearing options while not giving anything new to fill those holes.
I mostly wanted to see how big of a text box I could accumulate through requotes but also echo this sentiment.

If you're going to nerf these raid catch up items do it more subtely. Slightly reducing Bloodvine/LHH/Titanic DPS output through reducing the pure SP & STR of the items might make some sense but fully reworking them to have stamina changes the purpose of the items and homogenizes the gear available to players. Trust me, no one wants to use these items forever but they do serve an important role in the ecosystem by allowing an early 60 player the ability to get up the crucial hit rating necessary to do end game raiding but at a real cost, their health pool. I see that some of these changes have been slightly altered from the beginning and I believe that's at least a step in the right direction.

In regards to the Naxx trash drops. I think ilvl 80 would be a more appropriate nerf. In the case of the most egregious example, MSA, it would be slightly above R14 and slightly below Naxx boss drops. It's still not a sword so rogues will still seek to get CTS/AQR/R14 but would still leave it in the ranks of what it should be.. a weapon from the hardest content in the game.

I think the changes you make, in general, come off as quite transparently tailored to buff the hybrid classes you play and back hand the more specialized classes that you don't. Where is the ilvl 80 slow 1H sword? This seems like the biggest hole in vanilla itemization, period. A rogue must go from ilvl 77/78 to 89 with 0 opportunities in between.

Astrld, Nachichi, Snapcaster, Rafiq, Tazri

I understand the design intent behind the nerfs towards Naxx drops; However, I disagree with the blanket nerfs to pieces that will remain BiS even after the patch. I can't speak for every change, but the Ring of the Eternal Flame being nerfed from 34>29 accomplishes nothing, if not a flat 5sp nerf to mage BIS. It is a ring for mages, used exclusively by mages.

Exploring other gear set options with Labetha's Mage DPS Calculator (Such of Gloves of spell mastery/Pendant of the Faceless+Seal of the damned) still yields less DPS than the standard Mage BiS with a NERFED RotEF.

The change does not go far enough to shift BiS mages from using it, but I'd hesitate to advocate for a more extreme nerf. I think a far more practical solution would be to move the ring to Faerlina or another boss's loot-table. Or alternatively nerf the ring while buffing boss-drop alternatives.

author: Quidoba
subject: Re: 1.16.6 Itemization Changelog (Work In Progress)
content_md:
Itemization is hard, so I don't want to assume there are easy answers here.

In my opinion, TWOW should take the position that no itemization change should make pre-existing items swap place in anyone's BIS list. A very few new items can work their way in, but these should be rare. New items should be oriented as slightly worse options to the premier, but hard to get, items (like DFT, neth tear, etc).

Some items (like t1) can have their itemization improved so they are no longer irrelevant.  However, if items like Bloodvine are BIS through T3 for certain classes, then they should remain so in TWOW.  Give people more options, more ways to place different classes, but leave vanilla progression generally where it was in 1.12 (including catch-up tiers).

My justification:
I love wow, I love the community, but I'm done with the blizzard-style hamster wheel of gear progression.  I actually want stagnation of gear.  I want to explore new content in the gear I have, enjoy the lore, take month long breaks, make alts, farm gold, raid log if I want to but not feel forced into raiding.

I thought TWOW was the right place for this playstyle.  I thought it would weed out and not cater to the ADHD and gear obsessed. I liked that tmog and novelty items were added to inject more objectives without invalidating past work.  I have been exceedingly impressed with the take on Wow taken thus far.

I hope I'm wrong, but signs that things are going in the wrong direction include: ilevel focus, homogenation of gear, super linear progression.

If you want to make a fresh, phased, server, do that.  You can itemize your way into reproducing that.

In short - Please don't nerf gear people have already obtained.  Feels bad.
