> **Quidoba wrote: Tue Jul 25, 2023 12:46 pm**
> I love wow, I love the community, but I'm done with the blizzard-style hamster wheel of gear progression.  I actually want stagnation of gear.  I want to explore new content in the gear I have, enjoy the lore, take month long breaks, make alts, farm gold, raid log if I want to but not feel forced into raiding.

"Blizzard-style hamster wheel of gear progression" is the perfect description of what made me quit WoW a month into TBC. Realizing that everything you've worked for over months of raiding has become virtually meaningless and that this would happen again and again was massively off-putting to me. However! I think this is different. This is not raid gear being ilvl 80 and greens dropping from solo content in the new Hyjal zone being ilvl 95, completely invalidating the former. Your raid gear will still put you at a massive advantage over people who do not raid or who have just started raiding. The harshest nerfs are being dealt to craftable gear you can just pick up from the AH the moment you hit 60. I find it hard to apply the same reasoning (of not wanting your achievements of months of running raids being invalidated) to this kind of gear.
I even agree that some changes are fairly iffy when they don't just tone down the item but change its nature/role in caster itemization (like Bloodvine Boots losing +spell hit entirely.) But over all, the changes should leave you decently raid-viable. You can still use that gear, but now you can also eventually upgrade it. I don't think this is "forcing" you to raid either. You will still be a very powerful character after the gear changes.

> **Quidoba wrote: Tue Jul 25, 2023 12:46 pm**
> In my opinion, TWOW should take the position that no itemization change should make pre-existing items swap place in anyone's BIS list. A very few new items can work their way in, but these should be rare. New items should be oriented as slightly worse options to the premier, but hard to get, items (like DFT, neth tear, etc).

I agree with your position in general, but I'm not *that* much of a hardliner. The change to 2hand weapons adding feral AP depending on ilvl will massively upend every feral's BiS list. And I absolutely love it! It's fun and interesting, forces you to reevaluate preferences and gives you something to work towards, actually without introducing any new items at all.
I think it's completely fair to have a soft spot for iconic items like the BWL trinkets. But it's also pretty dumb that you can get a drop on your first run of BWL that you will never ever upgrade, effectively giving you a dead slot in terms of gear progression while you are still in the first third of raid progression (assuming you've gotten something like a Rejuvenating Gem off of Firemaw while your raid can't beat Chromaggus yet). It also makes the Vanilla+ aspect fairly hollow if all the additions could only ever be mid-tier content. I think new items being slightly more powerful or making slightly better use of the item budget should be fair game to not completely stall the game.

> **Quidoba wrote: Tue Jul 25, 2023 12:46 pm**
> Some items (like t1) can have their itemization improved so they are no longer irrelevant.  However, if items like Bloodvine are BIS through T3 for certain classes, then they should remain so in TWOW.  Give people more options, more ways to place different classes, but leave vanilla progression generally where it was in 1.12 (including catch-up tiers).

Yeah, this is actually a "problem" and one even harder to solve. TWoW introducing blue dungeon drops of ilvl 65 that make *very* good use of the item budget and in many cases outclass (the much more balanced) T1 pretty heavily is not very faithful to Vanilla. It is a bit strange to call out catch-up gear when a lot of custom dungeon drops are essentially that. I've run a lot of dungeons and before I've ever set foot into a raid I had around +600 healing on my gear, which is nuts. I have no idea how you can make the custom top-of-the-line dungeons interesting and attractive while maintaining a mostly Vanilla progression where T1 is actually a huge upgrade over T0 with a few dungeon drops mixed in. Because T1 into T2 works fairly well imo, so buffing T1 is probably not the solution and would require readjusting everything.

Some of the nerfs that have been announced so far seem a bit arbitrary and poorly thought out. Maybe they are. Or maybe we'll get a better picture when we get to know the drops from Karazhan Halls and Emerald Sanctum? Both shouldn't really be a problem for established raid groups of T2 or above, so hopefully the gaps in itemization can be filled fairly swiftly.

author: Mmoo
subject: Re: 1.16.6 Itemization Changelog (Work In Progress)
content_md: I disagree with changing **any** item that **already** have been in the game since the beginning (almost 20 years). While I understand why this is coming from, that generally raid items should be better than out-of-raid ones, the absolutely main issue here is that you are deflating all of the efforts that people already have put in to acquire those items. A better solution instead of making changes to the already existing, try to introduce even better alternatives and make people want to play the game even more, not less. And also make them feel that all of the effort they've put in was worthwhile and not fear for being actively deflated at some point in the future. This is a 1.12 forever server after all.

> **Elesion wrote: Tue Jul 25, 2023 2:42 pm**
> The harshest nerfs are being dealt to craftable gear you can just pick up from the AH the moment you hit 60. I find it hard to apply the same reasoning (of not wanting your achievements of months of running raids being invalidated) to this kind of gear.

I go back and forth on this.  Craftable gear can arguably be "harder" (as in take more effort) to get than t1 & t2 raid gear on a progressed server.  Alts or new recruits will get the raid gear easily by being mixed into a farm raid crew.  This is less true of t2.5 and naxx gear as only the most twinked guilds would consider these raids farmable enough to carry more than a couple loot babies.

Things like bloodvine actually land most classes/specs right in that sweet spot between t2 and t2.5, where they still have goals in t2 raids for premere items, and see replacements in AQ40 and naxx.  The gold/time invested in getting this catch-up gear is maybe lower than it should be, but it a cool objective for new players to work towards without submitting themselves to whims of a raiding guild.  It doesn't make sense to invalidate that effort by pointing to raids like MC and BWL as needing to be more rewarding.

The specific item that rubs me the wrong as a caster (maybe melee have something similar) is Rockfury bracers. This item being (significantly) better than Arcane Accuracy makes perfect sense to me.  After spending many weeks doing the tedious process of getting the rep and completing all the steps to get these bracers, it sucks to see the more casual raiders easily pick this up in BWL.

Again there's a lot more nuance to this discussion. It feels we could go on and on turning over every effect and side-effect.  Therefore, I would err on the side of caution.

Based on the current growing popularity of TWOW inspite of having Naxx out for years, I don't think the data would support Dragunovi's conclusion.  New players seem fine with things as they are. So why play with fire?

> **Chudman123 wrote: Fri Jul 28, 2023 5:34 am**
> notice all the above BG achievement awards have no real impact on PvE, this is on purpose so that PvP is not mandatory.

If you can shift that to a ring slot you free up space for another enchantment on boots (currently 7 sta/5 agi/5 spi; according to the changelog on the first page of this thread next patch will add 14 sta/12 spi/armor kits for 8 int + 6 sp). But we have to be honest that the proposed rewards would very much make PvE people salivate. Game balance is never as easy as you think it is   smiling_turtle_head

author: Aegaellian
subject: Re: 1.16.6 Itemization Changelog (Work In Progress)
content_md:
If you guys are just going to add back the Wolfsheart helm effect back as a lategame enchantment, why not just keep the item the way it is and make the new enchantment mutually exclusive with it so that lategame feral spec gets scaling and gear improvement but earlygame feral spec still keeps the iconic item?

I'm absolutely not a fan of the changes you guys are proposing this patch to iconic vanilla items because they're what make vanilla the way it is. There are tons of examples of outlier items that become iconic and exciting to obtain because they're big power boosts to your character that AREN'T prohibitive to obtain. In my opinion it's actually healthy for the game to have a few power items that are easy to obtain as they become exciting power spikes to work towards. "Smooth power progression" is one of the death-phrases that define retail World of Warcraft and there's a reason none of us are playing that. Classic World of Warcraft is filled with zany balancing and rewards which is the way lots of players like it. These changes are also punishing to players that don't or rarely raid as it literally strips power away from them with the compensation for most of these items being just "go raid, or else you won't have that power anymore." On that note I don't know why you guys are nerfing crafting, either. It would be interesting if there were MORE ways to gear up rather than less...crafting could have its own epic quests that sent you off on long adventures to craft gear in the same way that you can commit to raiding or PvP to obtain gear. Instead you guys are doing the opposite and neutering crafting for gear which is already in a pretty sorry state aside from very specific rep grind items and a couple power items which you guys are nerfing to the ground.

For me personally, I started playing on this server because it felt like Vanilla++, but the more changes happen to vanilla items the more the private-servery the game ends up feeling.

Not the change I would have expected for that item. content_html:
With the change to 1.17 and a supposedly "complete" change log I've gone over the post again with a fine toothed comb to add some thoughts and spot new changes. I won't repeat myself from previous pages on Lei or Ghoul Skin Tunic.
  • Deepearth Signet: Now Unique.
Not the change I would have expected for that item. It needs its stats changed, it's heavily under-budged for its ilvl (compare ilvl 65 Deepearth Signet to ilvl 60 Rosewine Circle. Making it unique pretends that people would love to run 2 of them. They don't, it's not a great ring. I've gone through the numbers in another thread and it's literally nowhere close to spending the budget of ilvl 65. Fix the stats and then it's completely sensible to make it unique.
  • Venom Covered Cloak: [386 Armor, +13 Stamina, +15 Nature Res, +3% Dodge] -> [167 Armor, +20 Stamina, +10 Nature Resist, +1% Resillience]
Good, that thing was broken as hell and inexplicably massively over budget (compare ilvl 77 Elementium Threaded Cloak to ivl 75 Venom Covered Cloak, the latter being massively better in literally every regard).
  • The Widow's Embrace: Item Level buffed from 81 to 83 for parity with other weapons from the same boss, increasing healing power gained from DPS Sacrifice. Increased healing power by 17.
I'm not opposed, but it does bring it weirdly close to Scepter of the False Prophet. Which should be no surprise as that is ilvl 84. I think Widow's Embrace at ilvl 81 was not some sort of oversight, it was to provide a gap to Scepter, which rightfully should be substantially more powerful coming from the final boss of a raid. Spider wing is the easiest in Naxx and doable for raids that fail at C'thun.
  • Noth's Frigid Heart: [+12 Intellect, +13 Spirit, +53 Healing] -> [+10 Intellect, +8 Spirit, +53 Healing, +5 MP5]
Very good change, this is now clearly more powerful than Sartura's Might, matching the discrepancy of 7 ilvls, when previously I would have slightly preferred Satura's Might.
  • Cap of the Scarlet Savant: [+17 Stamina, +20 Intellect, +2% Spell Crit] -> [+28 Intellect, +17 Stamina, +2% Spell Crit, +1% Spell Hit], Removed class restrictions.
  • Leggings of Arcana: [+20 Intellect, +30 Spirit, +18 Spellpower] -> [+17 Intellect, +20 Spirit, +32 Spellpower, +1% Spell Hit]
  • Breastplate of Bloodthirst: [+8 Intellect, +7 Fire Resistance, +9 MP5] -> [+14 Stamina, +12 Fire Resistance, +16 Spellpower]
These used to feel fairly weak compared to all the effort it took to get the materials. Not anymore. Still weird to find spell hit added when it was removed from other pre-raid gear because of "catch-up" concerns. It does mean that the caster gear doesn't provide its full power to healers anymore, when previously it did (spell hit is useless for healing). Should probably add a healing item to these books at some time.
  • Cooking:
    • Recipe: Gilnean Hot Stew (+12 Spellpower)
    • Recipe: Gurubashi Gumbo (+10 Stamina/+1% Reduced Chance to Get Crit)
    • Recipe: Le Fishe Au Chocolat (+3 Defense/+1% Dodge)
Very interesting. The "Gilnean" name makes me hope for an early caster food, which is filling a massive void in the cooking profession. Looking forward to it!
  • Diamond Flask: Spellpower scaling of the heal every 5 seconds component has been reduced from 1:1 for every healing tick to 1:0.1 for every tick. Strength buff reduced from 75 to 50 but cooldown has been reduced from 6 minutes to 4 minutes, allowing usage more often.

I'm fine with it, it is completely ridiculous for a trinket from Sunken Temple. Every other warrior I've matched with in Blood Ring had a +heal set and used the flask. I can see warriors loving their unique quirky mechanic and I actually feel for their loss and all the time invested into assembling their healing sets, but in a patch full of painful changes to other classes it seems the right time to address this once and for all. Kills something fun, but probably good for the balance in the long run.

author: Aegaellian
subject: Re: 1.17.0 Itemization Changelog
content_md:
What's the rationale behind the diamond flask change? I understand that it's an outlier item, but warrior is almost universally understood to be a class with incredibly limited agency for the vast majority of its leveling/gearing up process compared to almost every other class, in both PvP and PvE. If the issue was even with any specific game mode, it could be disabled there. But just removing a fun and notable item from the game, especially from a class that suffers the most for the majority of its gametime just feels bad. One of the very few moments of fun I had on my Warrior was when I got it and cobbled together a healing set, I could finally do maybe half of the things my shadowpriest, hunter, and warlock could do with similar gear. (t1-t1.5). Like I could maybe think about taking on an elite or two in PvE by myself without being in utter danger. In PvP it's useful, but countered by dispels and disabling CC. Against players who know how to play against it, it feels like there's actually interesting counterplay, rather than not having it and the pvp experience boiling down to basically being a binary "lol, a warrior that isn't geared in full naxx gear charged on me, I guess I just kill him", or, "wow, that warrior geared in full naxx gear charged on me and oneshot me before I could blink."

I definitely feel that because this is such a progressed server that the devs forget how some classes are played during progression rather than full BIS cap which is where Warriors finally shine, after months and months of grinding levels and endgame gear. Diamond flask was one of the only items that let warriors have a chance at having fun before that. All I can really say is that I'm both disappointed that an iconic vanilla item is being changed, and that a class that just isn't fun to play isn't receiving any changes to make it more fun to play, like Paladins have received. A flask change would have been welcomed if it was accompanied by any changes at all that gave Warriors any semblance of agency compared to other classes, but it didn't, it was actually accompanied by other item nerfs. If we're looking at how Blizzard eventually patched Diamond Flask's scaling ratio, we should also look at the fact that Warrior also eventually got QoL changes, and buffs to its agency and staying power to not feel so incredibly bad to play before being geared.

author: Aerocai
subject: Re: 1.17.0 Itemization Changelog
content_md:
In vanilla there's the argument that warriors endure being weak for 90% of their time spent leveling and gearing compared to other classes, but they're paid off for it by shining compared to everyone else in the lategame. You can't make that argument in TWoW, where many other classes have had sizable buffs to their dps and usability while warrior has received nothing but nerfs to the point that it's literally WORSE than its vanilla incarnation while every other class has received buffs. Out of all the class power curves, the most egregious example compared to warrior is probably hunter - in vanilla it's a class that's very easy to level, and is a powerhouse for most of its gametime, as well as being possibly the best class at soloing content and being self-sufficient, but they fall off due to poor scaling. Meanwhile in TWoW this never happens due to True Shot. It's actually really funny that my hunter's rotation which almost exclusively consists of auto shot -> true shot -> auto shot -> true shot does major competitive DPS in raids while being braindead easy and safe to play, on top of never having had to experience any pain that warrior has to.

Obviously tons of players have some kind of hateboner for warriors because yes endgame raid comps being just warriors is stupid, and t3 geared warriors are overwhelming in PvE and PvP. The solution to this is to smooth out the power curve of warrior by making lower geared warriors more playable and fun and higher geared warriors not so overwhelming, not by attacking power that lower geared warriors had access to (flask, lionheart helm, and other mid-tier gear) which makes playing and gearing warrior even MORE painful. Literally what's the point of playing warrior on this server when it's literally a worse incarnation of warrior than vanilla, on TOP of every other class being a better version of themselves from vanilla? If you nerf flask at least add back some other power that warriors below t3 can have access to. Prot tree is still hot garbage in both PvE and PvP. Gearing warriors still have garbage gear choices and are often half in leather which feels like absolute trash. There's literally no reason why warrior has to suffer because the old adage of "suffer until you're geared" doesn't make sense when other classes don't have to suffer nearly as much during the gearing process, and are also competitive when geared due to buffs.

IDK, adding new stuff to your server is nice and all but absolutely gutting literal vanilla items is imo where pservers go off the rails. Flask in particular is an item that makes you feel clever the same way people feel clever knowing that a small dinky quest from Gnomeregan gives you Triprunner Dungarees, which is a major power upgrade that can last 20-30 levels and should be gotten ASAP. Like why is Flask of all things being utterly gutted? Is it for Blood Ring? Just make it unusable in Blood Ring like Goblin Rocket Helm is unusable in Blood Ring. Absolutely gutting the scaling in all game modes just removes a fun item from the game from a class that rarely gets to shine before being super geared which feels utterly terrible, and that in a game where it's a serious mechanic to collect odds and ends for fun and to feel clever about, from Large Rope Nets to Magic Dust to engineering trinkets and on and on. On a server where there's the traditional classic balance, fine, but on a server where Paladins are having fun running around Holy Striking people for armor-piercing holy damage and a server where Hunters can get extremely competitive endgame DPS as well as being soloing machines that are easy to level, a server where Druids can get literal infinite mana from Blade of Eternal Darkness and on-hit effects, let my dinky t1 warrior have some vanilla fun with Flask, please. I don't want this to become a stiff "balanced" pserver just because it got popular, because that clearly wasn't what I signed up for with how much crazy stuff you can do on this server.

author: Aegaellian
subject: Re: 1.17.0 Itemization Changelog
content_md:
Druids with Blade of Eternal Darkness with custom server on-hit build getting infinite mana = All smiles
Warriors with vanilla Diamond flask with healing power set = No, not allowed.

The weirdest thing is that in older TWoW design, the devs have embraced outlier items, so tons of the changes this patch are literally an about-face design choice, but only partially, and only directed towards certain classes. For example, it's an outlier that Wolfshead Helm is literally BiS forever for ferals in vanilla, so they're changing it. But Manual Crowd Pummeler is also an outlier item for both ret pallies and druids. What did the turtle wow devs do with that item? They literally SUPPORTED its outlier status with hypertech battery pack and the craftable version of Crowd Pummeler. Like WTF, at least be consistent? This is why it's so jarring that you guys are now coming up with knee-jerk nerfs when all things pointed to the server supporting outlier items, like with on-hit druids and paladins, and other unique items and builds, and now you're going in the other direction "balancing" things.

author: Dragunovi
subject: Alternative Tier Sets
content_md:
**Greetings! Today we're happy to announce that alternative class armor sets are in the works and slated for release in **1.17.2: Tower of Karazhan**!**

These armor sets allow specializations that struggle with itemization to swap their tier pieces to versions that are tailored towards their preferred version, **complete with all new set bonuses**. If you plan on getting multiple Legacy sets with the intention of changing one of them into its alternative version, make sure to put the Legacy tier set items you want to keep using in your bank as to avoid losing enchantments.

 **Tier 1, 2 and Tier 3 (Rings Only)** gear pieces will be swappable to their alternative counterparts via new quests while you'll need to use the new quest reward swapper NPC introduced in 1.17.2 for Tier 2.5 and 3, meaning you can convert your existing sets using this NPC as the original quests for Tier 2.5 and Tier 3 are now a reward choice between the original set and the alternative set(s), Tier 3.5 won't be available to be swapped using this NPC, pick your set wisely!
In addition, Tier 1 and 2 will be **recolors** of their original sets to further differentiate them.

You can find the details below:
- Specializations listed with a / share the armor set.

- There will be different alternative Tier 2.5 sets for some classes due to existing versions already being tailored towards DPS.

- **Legacy Warlock** and **Hunter** sets have had their set bonuses updated to accomodate for Fire Destruction and Survival specializations and their abilities.
The following specializations will get new alternative tier sets:
- Mage: Arcane

- Priest: Shadow (Tier 1, 2 and 3), Holy (Tier 2.5 Only), Smite (Tier 2.5 Only, Original Tier 2.5 has been converted into the new Smite set while there is a new Holy set for Tier 2.5)

- Warrior: Arms/Fury (Tier 1, 2 and 3, the reason for there being none for Tier 2.5 and 3.5 is that they're hybridized to work for both threat generation oriented tanking and damage dealing.)

- Warlock: Affliction

- Druid: Feral Combat (Tier 1, 2.5 and 3.5 are Cat Form DPS focused while Tier 2 and 3 are Bear Form Tanking focused), Balance (Legacy Tier 2.5 is the new Balance set while there is a new Restoration set for Tier 2.5), Restoration (Tier 2.5 Only)

- Shaman: Enhancement (Tier 2.5 is specialized for tanking builds), Elemental (Legacy Tier 2 and 2.5 are the new Elemental sets while there are new Restoration sets for Tier 2 and 2.5.

- Paladin: Retribution, Protection, Holy (Tier 2.5 now has a new item set while Tier 1 and 2 have been re-itemized to work better for Holy Paladins as the specializations using them previously now have new alternative tier sets.)
Thanks for reading!

  • Warrior: Arms/Fury (Tier 1, 2 and 3, the reason for there being none for Tier 2.5 and 3.5 is that they're hybridized to work for both threat generation oriented tanking and damage dealing.)
  • Warlock: Affliction
  • Druid: Feral Combat (Tier 1, 2.5 and 3.5 are Cat Form DPS focused while Tier 2 and 3 are Bear Form Tanking focused), Balance (Legacy Tier 2.5 is the new Balance set while there is a new Restoration set for Tier 2.5), Restoration (Tier 2.5 Only)
  • Shaman: Enhancement (Tier 2.5 is specialized for tanking builds), Elemental (Legacy Tier 2 and 2.5 are the new Elemental sets while there are new Restoration sets for Tier 2 and 2.5.
  • Paladin: Retribution, Protection, Holy (Tier 2.5 now has a new item set while Tier 1 and 2 have been re-itemized to work better for Holy Paladins as the specializations using them previously now have new alternative tier sets.)
Thanks for reading!

author: Elesion
subject: Re: Alternative tier sets & midpatch itemization changes
content_md:
> **Dragunovi wrote: Sun Oct 15, 2023 10:51 pm**
> The existing tier sets that drop from bosses will now be classified as **Legacy**, which keep their current stats, set bonuses, appearances and serve as tokens that are turned in to acquire these alternative sets.
>
> - Druid: Feral Combat (Cat/Bear), Balance, Restoration (Tier 2.5 Only)

I appreciate the idea, especially since it gives ferals an actual item progression into Naxx. But I can definitely see some challenges.

Cats and bears have almost opposite stat weights. Raid cats want to be glass cannons (like dps warriors often run leather gear) while raid bears need to be beefy and tanky (like tank warriors in +def plate). Putting both on the same set will not be an easy task. The Convergence of the Elements set tried that and ended up with a weird mix of half of the items being tank-geared and the other half dps-geared, just being carried by the set bonus because individually nobody would run all 4 pieces at the same time.

Hard to tell without seeing the proposed sets, but if they end up being fully optimized towards their respective specs, the Legacy sets may feel very weak in comparison. T1 is already hybridized into Balance (items with damage/healing, set bonuses for spell crit and boosting Hurricane). T2 also has some weirdly un-optimized pieces (Boots and Chest with spell crit eating up a lot of item budget while not doing a whole lot for druid healing). If the goal is to untangle specs and give each an optimized set you might consider updating the Resto-oriented Legacy sets as well.

Given what happened to Genesis (T2.5), the push towards 3 separate sets for every tier, and here the rework of AQ20 and T0.5 - Without seeing the final stats I have to assume there are no plans for a hybrid set? I agree they have very limited use in PvE, but something to support a more hybrid PvP build would be nice. There was already a little bit of backlash on changing Genesis and while I found that set beyond useless, I can see why some people liked it. Wildheart/Feralheart is very similar to how Genesis used to be.

Great change, but unless you ban t2.5 and t3 from pvp, you're basically giving the pvp server a 1 year lifespan, until people are running around with t3. A full t3 elemental shaman? Basically every spell is a one-shot unless you're flasked and enchanted with stamina?

Full t3 paladin??

As a Prot Paladin, I cant tell you how many times ive seen Warrior T1 drop and say
"Dangit, I wish my set had Defense or X stat"

But this got me thinking and id like to share some thoughts with the Devs.

Many discussions with other prot pallys and raid leaders basically saying

author: Shambakriger
subject: Re: Alternative Tier Sets & Midpatch Itemization Changes
content_md:
I do hope this change won’t encourage all classes/specs to go 8/8 on all tier sets though. I’m probably in the minority, but as a feral main I’ve always quite enjoyed the hybrid gearing process.
I’d prefer a system of smaller sets like the AQ20, ZG and various crafted ones, utilising both the same slots as T1-3 but also off-slots like the AQ20 set (finger, back, weap)
Preferably with big, gameplay-altering set bonuses, locked behind 2/3 and 4/5. Locking BiS set bonuses behind 8/8 feels a bit boring to me, as it stops the player from mixing and matching their gear how they want.
So my hopes for the new tier sets is for the 8/8 bonus to be extremely flavourful, but underperforming compared to the mix-and-match gearing of most classes atm.
An example could be an 8/8 set bonus for ferals that massively buffed a bleeds/dot playstyle, but still fell short of bis cat dps gear. So the player gets to choose whether they want to go for 8/8 or maybe mix-and-match with a 3/8 from another tier set.

Hope it makes sense:3
No matter how you end up designing it I’ll look forward to trying it out! 1.17 was absolutely amazing and has me so hyped for the future of twow<3

author: Elesion
subject: Re: Alternative Tier Sets & Midpatch Itemization Changes
content_md:
> **Nallkun wrote: Sun Jan 07, 2024 2:38 pm**
> Super looking forward to these Alternate Tier sets...
>  They were announced roughly 3 months ago (Oct 15th 2023) - Do we have any kinda sorta ballpark?  Next Major patch? or slipped in One Tuesday randomly?

My understanding is that there has been work done on them around the time they were announced, even some of them created. But then the developers realized that it would be foolish to release them at this point.

There is a long-standing project called "Class Changes 2". Using volunteers from the community the developers want to address issues the various classes have and generally try to achieve better balance. We're looking at fixes, changes to spells and abilities, reworks of talent trees, etc. Applications for the volunteer positions were sent in many months ago but it turned out to be many hundreds so they are still under review as far as I know.

The problem with releasing alternate tier sets is now twofold:
 1) The set bonuses might go in the same direction as Class Changes 2. After all problems or shortcoming a class might have can be addressed through powerful set bonuses or by reworking the class. So either the subsequent Class Changes would then double up (making the set bonus useless) or would have to avoid fixing the issues the sets have already addressed (which seems shortsighted).
 2) The set bonuses and stat weights might also go in opposite directions. If the Class Changes 2 happen to introduce substantial changes, the set bonuses or item stats might no longer be in high demand.

So my understanding is that alternate tier sets have been shelved indefinitely until Class Changes 2 are done, so the new items can be tailored to the "final" state of the classes.

author: Dogfight
subject: Re: Alternative Tier Sets & Midpatch Itemization Changes
content_md:
Some quick thoughts about alternate tier sets for paladins in hope to influence the prosess before it is done:

Previously leaked screenshots of T3 ret gear shows that it is AP focused. Imo ret gear should be hybrid like T2,5. We use mana as resource, so it makes more sense with regards to class fantasy to have gear with int and SP.  Else class changes has to give us a way to regen mana reliably. Not fun to play when you run out of mana, cannot use abilities and cannot regen to keep consistency/longevity like other classes. Mana management still has to be part of the playstyle, but not being able to use your toolkit/max rank spells over duration of a fight is something that should be fixed.

As for prot gear we gave feedback to Ques that stam, int and agi were the primary stats we wanted. However, that was before Class changes 2 were planned and is likely outdated now. Hopefully prot tree will be improved enough to make Vengeance not mandatory for threat. That also makes agility on tank gear unnecessary and can focus on stam/int/sp instead to build a SP based tank that has good threat without it being based on crits to trigger vengeance. We can get avoidance as dodge % instead.

Lastly; would be Nice to get an update on how to aquire T3 alternate sets. I have 8 tokens gathering dust in my bank. Worth to get Holy T3 for OS now and then turn it in for ret/prot T3 later, or will the tokens be handed in as today but for alternate sets? Would be Nice to get an update on this soon. Would be better for the economy as well that we get to know, in case T3,5 also requires crafting materials.

subject: Re: Alternative Tier Sets
content_md:
You can exchange t1&t2 tokens at the blackrock.

Those alt versions of T1, T2 as well as the
T2.5 & T3 pieces are quest rewards. Like other questrewards, they can now be swapped at a npc in Ratchet.

Do beware, the Ratchet NPC is ruthless and will rip them off of your character without a second confirmation - replacing a potentially enchanted piece of gear with a new unenchanted one.

Also T1 &T2 tokens can not be turned back into their original form once traded. You will have to farm the original piece again

subject: Midpatch Itemization Changes Changelog
content_md:
Greetings! We're happy to announce that the **Midpatch Itemization Changes** (or M.I.C. for short) are now complete and went live with scheduled maintenance!
Do keep in mind we will be monitoring the items and their performances and might do future adjustments as needed. You can see the list of changes below:

 **Dungeon Set 2/Tier 0.5 Rework:**
All pieces of the set are now item level 60 epics. This affects the item level 65-66 blues and the item level 55 epic gloves for all sets, increasing their stat budget.
In addition, some other pieces have seen some slight tweaks to make them more worthwhile to acquire.

- Warrior:
 - Bracers of Heroism: 9 -> 10 Strength, 5 -> 10 Agility

 - Belt of Heroism: 9 -> 12 Agility, Added 1% Hit

 - Spaulders of Heroism: 12 -> 13 Agility and Strength, Added 1% Hit

 - Legplates of Heroism: 11 -> 16 Agility, Added 1% Critical Chance

 - Gauntlets of Heroism: 18 -> 20 Strength, 12 -> 14 Stamina

- Rogue:
 - Darkmantle Bracers: 7 -> 10 Strength, 7 -> 10 Stamina

 - Darkmantle Belt: 13 -> 16 Stamina, 10 -> 15 Strength

 - Darkmantle Spaulders: 10 -> 12 Stamina, Added 1% Hit

 - Darkmantle Pants: 15 -> 17 Stamina, 15 -> 16 Strength, Added 1% Critical Chance

 - Darkmantle Gloves: 12 -> 13 Strength, 9 -> 13 Stamina

- Paladin:
 - Soulforge Bracers: Added 9 Agility

 - Soulforge Belt: 10 -> 11 Strength, 11 -> 12 Stamina, 12 -> 15 Spellpower, Removed 4 MP5, Added 1% Critical Chance

 - Soulforge Spaulders: 10 -> 12 Strength, 12 -> 15 Spellpower,  Added 1% Hit and 11 Agility

 - Soulforge Legplates: 12 -> 15 Spellpower, Added 1% Critical Chance

 - Soulforge Gauntlets: 11 -> 15 Spellpower, 10 -> 11 Stamina and Intellect, 9 -> 11 Strength

- Priest:
 - Virtuous Bracers: 8 -> 9 All Stats, 9 -> 13 Spellpower

 - Virtuous Belt: 12 -> 14 Spellpower, Added 1% Spell Hit

 - Virtuous Mantle: 12 -> 16 Spellpower, Added 5 MP5

 - Virtuous Skirt: 13 -> 15 Stamina, 12 -> 15 Spirit, 14 -> 16 Intellect, 16 -> 24 Spellpower, Added 1% Spell Hit

 - Virtuous Gloves: Added 1% Spell Hit

 - Virtuous Crown: 11 -> 18 Spellpower

 - Virtuous Robe: 21 -> 17 Stamina, 22 -> 16 Intellect, 14 -> 24 Spellpower, Added 1% Spell Critical Chance

- Mage:
 - Sorcerer's Bindings: 8 -> 14 Spellpower, 8 -> 10 Stamina

 - Sorcerer's Belt: 14 -> 16 Spellpower, Added 1% Spell Hit

 - Sorcerer's Leggings: 16 -> 24 Spellpower, Added 1% Spell Crit

 - Sorcerer's Mantle: 9 -> 20 Spellpower

 - Sorcerer's Gloves: 12 -> 14 Spellpower

 - Sorcerer's Robes: 25 -> 18 Intellect, 16 -> 28 Spellpower, Replaced 20 Spell Penetration with 1% Spell Hit

 - Sorcerer's Crown: 25 -> 17 Intellect, 14 -> 11 Spirit, 11 -> 26 Spellpower

- Warlock:
 - Deathmist Bracers: Increased Spellpower from 8 to 13.

 - Deathmist Belt: Added 1% Spell Spell Critical Chance.

 - Deathmist Mantle: Increased Spellpower from 12 to 19.

 - Deathmist Leggings: Reduced Intellect from 21 to 20, Reduced Stamina from , 16 -> 24 Spellpower, Added 1% Spell Hit.

 - Deathmist Wraps: 13 -> 16 Intellect, 13 -> 14 Spellpower

 - Deathmsit Robe: 22 -> 18 Intellect, 27 -> 23 Stamina, 12 -> 25 Spellpower

 - Deathmist Mask: 24 -> 19 Stamina and Intellect, 16 -> 26 Spellpower

- Hunter:
 - Beastmaster's Bindings: Increased Agility from 16 to 18, Increased Stamina from 7 to 8, Increased Intellect from 5 to 7.

 - Beastmaster's Belt: Increased Agility from 16 to 17, Added 1% Hit

 - Beastmaster's Mantle: Added 1% Crit

 - Beastmaster's Pants: Increased Stamina from 14 to 16, Increased Intellect from 9 to 12, Added 1% Crit

 - Beastmaster's Gloves: Added 1% Hit

- Shaman:
 - Bindings of The Five Thunders: Removed Strength, Increased Spellpower from 8 to 13, Added 4 MP5.

 - Cord of The Five Thunders: Removed Strength, Increased Spellpower from 12 to 15, Increased MP5 from 4 to 5, Added 1% Spell Hit.

 - Pauldrons of The Five Thunders: Removed Strength and Agility, Increased Spellpower from 12 to 18, Increased Stamina from 13 to 15, Added 4 MP5.

 - Kilt of The Five Thunders: Removed Strength and Agility, Increased Stamina from 12 to 16, Increased Spellpower from 18 to 24, Added 1% Spell Hit and 5 MP5.

 - Gauntlets of The Five Thunders: Removed Strength, Increased Spellpower from 12 to 14, Added 1% Spell Crit.

 - Boots of The Five Thunders: Removed Strength and Agility, Increased Intellect from 10 to 13, Increased Spellpower from 12 to 14, Added 1% Spell Hit.

 - Coif of The Five Thunders: Removed Strength and Agility, Increased Spellpower from 18 to 24, Added 5 MP5.

 - Vest of The Five Thunders: Removed Strength and Agility, Increased Spellpower from 18 to 26, Added 4 MP5.

- Druid:
 - The set has been renamed to **Moonheart** and this change is only reflected on the items for now, the set name and set bonus adjustments to make them fully caster oriented will be done with a future client update.

 - Feralheart Bracers: 12 Intellect, 7 Spirit, 8 Stamina, 14 Spellpower

 - Feralheart Belt: 14 Intellect, 11 Spirit, 12 Stamina, 13 Spellpower, 1% Spell Hit

 - Feralheart Spaulders: 14 Intellect, 13 Spirit, 12 Stamina, 18 Spellpower

 - Feralheart Kilt: 18 Intellect, 15 Spirit, 15 Stamina, 24 Spellpower, 1% Spell Hit

 - Feralheart Gloves: 15 Intellect, 11 Spirit, 12 Stamina, 12 Spellpower, 1% Spell Hit

 - Feralheart Boots: 12 Intellect, 12 Spirit, 12 Stamina, 14 Spellpower, 1% Spell Crit

 - Feralheart Cowl: 17 Intellect, 14 Spirit, 15 Stamina, 24 Spellpower, 1% Spell Crit

 - Feralheart Vest: 20 Intellect, 10 Spirit, 16 Stamina, 24 Spellpower, 1% Spell Crit

Mage Tier 1 and 2 Updates:
We've taken a second look at the itemization on these sets and have done some adjustments to bring them on par with other better options that became available later during the Vanilla patch cycle.

 **Tier 1 (Arcanist Regalia):**
- Head:
 27 Intellect -> 25 Intellect
 10 Spirit -> 8 Spirit
 20 Spell Damage -> 26 Spell Damage

- Shoulder:
 21 Intellect -> 16 Intellect
 10 Stamina -> 13 Stamina
Removed Spirit
Removed Mp5
 14 Spell Damage -> 18 Spell Damage
Added 1 Spell Crit

- Chest:
 25 Intellect -> 21 Intellect
 19 Stamina -> 16 Stamina
Removed Spirit
Added 1 Spell Hit
 23 Spell Damage -> 30 Spell Damage

- Bracers:
 8 Stamina -> 10 Stamina
 6 Spirit -> 5 Spirit
Removed Mp5
 12 Spell Damage -> 16 Spell Damage

- Gloves:
 15 Intellect -> 17 Intellect
 14 Stamina -> 14 Stamina
 10 Spirit -> 12 Spirit
Removed Mp5
 14 Spell Damage -> 19 Spell Damage

- Waist:
 20 Intellect -> 18 Intellect
Added 1 Spell Hit

- Leggings:
Unchanged.

- Boots:
 14 Intellect ->  16 Intellect
 11 Spirit -> 9 Spirit
 11 Spell Damage -> 14 Spell Damage
 **Tier 2 (Netherwind Regalia):**

- Head:
Added 1 Spell Crit.
 7 Spirit -> 11 Spirit
Removed MP5.

- Shoulder:
 13 Intellect -> 15 Intellect
 12 Spirit -> 10 Spirit
Removed MP5.
Added 1 Spell Hit.
 21 Spell Damage -> 23 Spell Damage

- Chest:
Unchanged.

- Bracers:
 9 Stamina -> 11 Stamina
Removed MP5.
 19 Spell Damage -> 21 Spell Damage

- Gloves:
Removed Spirit.
 20 Spell Damage -> 22 Spell Damage

- Belt:
 20 Intellect -> 18 Intellect
 13 Spirit -> 8 Spirit
Added 1 Spell Hit.

- Legs:
Unchanged.

- Boots:
Unchanged.
AQ20 Set Reworks:
All set weapons' item level has been increased from 70 to 74 and turned into Uniques, increasing their stats and DPS/Healing Power/Spellpower and only allowing one per character as a result. We've also adjusted stats on a few pieces to make them worth the trip to the Ruins of Ahn'Qiraj.

- Hunter:
 - Scythe of the Unseen Path: Reduced Agility from 16 to 14. Reduced Stamina from 9 to 6. Replaced 3 MP5 with 1% Physical Critical Chance.

 - Signet of the Unseen Path: Reduced Agility from 19 to 17. Increased Stamina from 11 to 12. Removed Intellect. Added 1% Physical Hit Chance.

- Warrior:
 - Sickle of Unyielding Strength: Damage values increased to 81 - 151.

- Priest:
 - Gavel of Infinite Wisdom: Increased MP5 from 4 to 5. Increased Healing Power from 90 to 106.

 - Ring of Infinite Wisdom: Increased MP5 from 4 to 5. Reduced Intellect from 13 to 9. Reduced Stamina 10 to 8. Added 29 Healing Power.

 - Shroud of Infinite Wisdom: Reduced Intellect from 14 to 11. Reduced Stamina from 12 to 8. Reduced Spirit from 11 to 10. Added 5 MP5.

- Mage:
 - Blade of Vaulted Secrets: Increased Spellpower from 40 to 56.

 - Drape of Vaulted Secrets: Increased Intellect from 9 to 10. Reduced Stamina from 14 to 13. Removed Spirit. Increased Spellpower from 18 to 22.

- Paladin:
 - Blade of Eternal Justice: Damage values increased to 73 - 137. Intellect reduced from 8 to 7. Stamina reduced from 16 to 14.

 - Cape of Eternal Justice: Stamina reduced from 13 to 9. Added 1% Haste.

 - Ring of Eternal Justice: Reduced Intellect from 12 to 9. Reduced Stamina from 11 to 7. Increased Spellpower from 13 to 15. Added 1% Physical Hit Chance.

- Rogue:
 - Dagger of Veiled Shadows: Damage values increased to 69 - 130.

 - Band of Veiled Shadows: Reduced Agility from 18 to 17. Added 1% Haste.

- Warlock:
 - Kris of Unspoken Names: Spellpower increased from 59 to 71. Increased Stamina from 9 to 13.

- Druid:
 - Mace of Unending Life: Damage values adjusted to 100 - 188. Added 50 Armor and 1% Dodge. Increased Feral Attack Power from 140 to 196.

 - Cloak of Unending Life: Removed Intellect, Spirit and Spellpower. Reduced Strength from 12 to 10. Added 16 Attack Power and 1% Physical Critical Strike Chance.

 - Band of Unending Life: Removed Intellect and Spirit. Increased Stamina from 9 to 13. Increased Agility from 10 to 13. Added 1% Haste.

- Shaman:
 - Hammer of the Gathering Storm: Removed Strength. Increased Spellpower from 53 to 64. Added 1% Spell Critical Chance.

 - Cloak of the Gathering Storm: Removed Strength. Reduced Intellect from 13 to 10. Reduced Stamina from 10 to 9. Increased Spellpower from 14 to 18. Added 1% Spell Hit Chance.

 - Ring of the Gathering Storm: Removed Strength and Agility. Increased Spellpower from 12 to 20.
 **Steel Plate Armor Adjustments:**
The Steel Plate pieces have seen some adjustments, correcting their lackluster item levels to be the baseline required level + 5 values and adjusting their stats accordingly.

- Steel Plate Barbute: Item level adjusted to 50. Increased Armor from 426 to 510. Decreased Stamina from 17 to 15. Increased Strength from 9 to 10. Added 1% Dodge.

- Steel Plate Pauldrons: Item level adjusted to 50. Decreased Stamina from 14 to 12. Removed 1% Dodge.

- Steel Plate Legguards: Item level adjusted to 50. Increased Defense from 2 to 3.

- Steel Plate Boots: Item level adjusted to 48. Decreased Stamina from 11 to 10. Decreased Strength from 10 to 9. Increased Armor from 322 to 334.

- Steel Plate Gauntlets: Item level adjusted to 49. Decreased Stamina from 15 to 12. Decreased Strength from 8 to 7. Added 2 Defense.

- Steel Plate Armor: Item level adjusted to 50. Decreased Stamina from 15 to 14. Increased Strength from 9 to 10. Decreased Defense from 5 to 4.
 **Hateforge Armor Rework:**
The Hateforge Blacksmithing Armor Set has been reworked to become a full blown haste centric set.

All the pieces are now Bind on Equip and can be traded amongst players and sold on the Auction House, including the epic Hateforge Grips.

- Hateforge Grips: Increased Strength from 9 to 13. Removed 1% Haste.

- Hateforge Belt: Reduced Strength from 20 to 15. Changed 13 Spirit to 15 Stamina. Added 1% Haste.

- Hateforge Boots: Reduced Strength from 17 to 13. Increased Stamina from 5 to 13. Removed Spirit. Added 1% Haste.

- Hateforge Cuirass: Increased Strength from 10 to 18. Increased Haste from 1% to 2%.

- Hateforge Leggings: Increased Strength from 19 to 22. Increased Stamina from 10 to 13. Added 1% Physical Hit Chance.

- Hateforge Helmet: Increased Strength from 18 to 19. Increased Stamina from 7 to 19. Added 1% Haste and 1% Resillience.
 **Armor Penetration Adjustment:**
The Armor Penetration stat's value has been doubled from 0.2 to 0.4, meaning current items will have their armor penetration amounts halved. The changes go as follows:
- 100 Armor Penetration -> 50 Armor Penetration:
 - Breastplate of Earthen Might

 - Band of Calamity

 - Bone Fracture

 - Chimaera's Eye

 - Giants Heavy Mace

 - Tooth of the Packlord

- 75 Armor Penetration -> 40 Armor Penetration:
 - Mark of the Worgen

 - Corrosive Core

- 75 Armor Penetration -> 35 Armor Penetration:
 - Shieldbreaker Arbalest

- 50 Armor Penetration -> 25 Armor Penetration:
 - Dark Iron Destroyer

 - Darkflame Helm

 - Dreamsteel Leggings

 - Earthbreaker Belt

 - Nature's Call

 - Sabatons of the Endless March

 - Sandstalker's Shroud

 - Coldheart Icicle

 - Deepstone Boots

 - Rune of Duty (Level 40 Version)

 - Slateplate Leggings

 - Apefist Pummelers

 - Golden Scale Coif

 - Sharp Teeth Necklace

- 40 Armor Penetration -> 20 Armor Penetration
 - Shawl of Haunted Memories

 - Pulverizer Gauntlets

 - Blackhammer Pauldrons

- 30 Armor Penetration -> 15 Armor Penetration
 - Granitized Bracers

 - Golden Scale Cuirass

 - Rune of Duty (Level 20 Version)

 - Golden Scale Leggings

- 20 Armor Penetration -> 10 Armor Penetration
 - Dreamsteel Boots

 - Sentinel's Glaive

 - Golden Scale Bracers

 - Golden Scale Gauntlets

- Armor Penetration Removed
 - Sentinel's Breastplate

 - Sentinel's Crown

 - Sentinel's Leggings
 **Shady Rest Inn Quest Rewards Update:**
All rewards' item level updated to item level 47, increasing stats, armor, block and DPS. Additionally we've adjusted the itemization on these items to make them more viable.

- Wattapo's Bulwark and Dustwallow Defender: Removed 10 Nature Resistance, Replaced 5 Spirit with 7 Stamina.

- Brackenwall Longbow and Theramore Arbalest: Increased Agility from 3 to 8.

- Stonemaul Seer Club: No longer gives any stats, instead grants 1% Spell Hit.

- Ornate Dagger of Jalvan: Increased Intellect from 3 to 6, Increased Spellpower from 7 to 9.

- Krog's Pike: Increased Strength from 12 to 20, Increased Stamina from 8 to 14.

- Garran's Pike: Increased Strength from 16 to 20, Added 1% Crit.
 **Gilneas Quest Rewards Update:**
Some rewards have been updated to properly fit in the stat budget.

- Dark Footpad Belt: Increased Strength from 13 to 15, Increased Agility from 5 to 10.

- Blackthorn Gauntlets: Increased Stamina from 4 to 6, Increased Agility from 2 to 6, Increased Spirit from 1 to 7, Increased Vampirism from 1% to 2%.

- Signet of Gilneas: Increased Stamina from 4 to 11.

- Ravenshire Gloves: Increased Spirit and Stamina from 7 to 9.

- Varimathras' Cunning: Increased Intellect from 12 to 18, Increased Spirit from 5 to 8.

- Stillward Amulet: Added 1% Haste.

- Garalon's Might: Increased Strength from 18 to 21, Replaced 13 Intellect with 1% Haste.
 **Hyjal Quest Rewards Update:**
Some rewards have been updated to properly fit in the stat budget.

- Gladeforge Breastplate: Increased Stamina from 23 to 25, Increased Agility from 12 to 15.

- Dreamwind Sigil: Reduced Nature and Shadow Resistance from 12 to 10.

- Moonseeker Staff: Item Level increased from 62 to 65, increasing DPS roughly from 48 to 50. Haste increased from 1% to 2%.

- Talisman of the Dreamshaper: Increased Nature Resistance from 3 to 5.

- Defender of Nordrassil: Increased Intellect from 4 to 6, Increased Stamina from 2 to 6, Replaced 16 Holy Spellpower with 7 Nature Spellpower.

- Clutch of Renewal: Replaced 24 Nature Spellpower with 20 Normal Spellpower.

- Dreamwind Spaulders: Reduced Spellpower from 22 to 19, Removed 7 Nature Spellpower.

- Windtalker Cape: Reduced Strength from 16 to 15, Removed 10 Nature Resistance.

- Cuffs of Nordanaar: Removed Intellect and Spirit, Increased Agility from 7 to 10.

- Groveslicer Glaive: Increased Strength from 7 to 9, Increased Nature Resistance from 3 to 5, Changed damage values from 88 - 133 to 76 - 142 (DPS remains the same).
 **Miscellaneaous:**
- Lasher's Whip now properly binds to the player upon pickup.

- Fixed double Intellect stat on Ancient Jade Leggings.

- Axe of Dormant Slumber, Vampiris Kris, Ring of Nature's Duality, Vial of Potent Venoms and Medivh's Foresight are now Unique.

- Reduced Intellect on Dawnstone Hammer from 32 to 25.

- Fixed Armor value on Leggings of the Shrouding Mists.

- Reduced Strength and Stamina on Anasterian's Legacy from 16 to 12.

- Fixed Dark Iron Reaver's equip spell to properly function and have the proper effect.

- Reduced the Haste of Wing of the Time-Lord from 2% to 1%. Increased Strength and Agility from 11 to 12 and the Stamina from 8 to 11.

- Fixed Spellweaver's Turban stats as per told in the patchnotes.

- Fixed sheathing on the Spear of the Endless Hunt.

- Slightly buffed Shield of Mathela and Sword of Laneron.

- Fixed the unusually high armor value on Boarskin Cloak.

- Dwarven Battle Bludgeon's stun effect has been changed to a proc instead of being an on use effect.

- Added 1% Spell Hit Chance to the Ring of Nature's Duality. The previous nerfs in the last changelog were excessive, so we have decided to restore some offensive power to the ring.

- Decreased Haste from 2% to 1% and increased Stamina from 10 to 13 for the Sanctum Bark Wraps.

- The Nemesis Gloves should now have the reworked stats as specified in the patch changelog.

- The Strength and Stamina values on the Thick Obsidian Breastplate have been swapped.

- The Magus Blade no longer deals Arcane damage on swings.

- Decreased Strength from 31 to 26 and increased Stamina from 4 to 13 for the Dreamsteel Boots.

- Changed 14 Agility to Stamina and 1% Vampirism to 1% Physical Hit Chance for the Dreamsteel Leggings.

- Decreased Intellect from 26 to 19, removed 5% Meditation, and added 19 Spellpower to the Dreamthread Mantle.

- Reduced Strength from 33 to 25 and changed Agility to Stamina, increasing it from 12 to 15, Removed 1% Haste and 12 Attack Power, and added 1% Critical Chance to Dreamsteel Mantle.

- Shoulders crafted from Dream materials (Dreamthread, Dreamsteel, Dreamhide) now require a profession skill of 300 to equip, as they are much stronger than other pieces in their sets.

- Fixed damage values on Axe of the Wildtusk.

- Band of Infinite Possibilities now provides a flat 18 spellpower instead of a range of 1-36 spellpower. This change was made because the spellpower value is randomized per equip, not per cast.

- Fixed the feral attack power bonus on the Grand Marshal's Glaive and High Warlord's Pig Sticker.

- Maladath, Runed Blade of the Black Flight: Increased +Swords from 4 to 5.

- Magnetic Band: Increased Intellect from 3 to 5, Increased Spirit from 2 to 5.

- Towerforge Breastplate: Increased Strength from 20 to 23, Increased Stamina from 23 to 28, Reduced Critical Chance from 2% to 1%.

- Towerforge Crown: Reduced Haste from 2% to 1%, Replaced 1% Critical Chance with 1% Hit.

- Towerforge Pauldrons: Reduced Strength from 17 to 15, Replaced 1% Critical Chance with 1% Hit.

- Boreal Mantle: Increased Intellect from 8 to 11, Increased Stamina from 5 to 6, Reduced Frost Spellpower from 29 to 24.

author: Quidoba
subject: Re: Midpatch Itemization Changes Preliminary Changelog
content_md:
> **Kharkov72 wrote: Wed Oct 18, 2023 9:03 pm**
> those aq20 weapons seems kinda overbuffed, being as good if not better than bwl-aq40 weapons. i do think they need a buff, but not THAT much

Yea, you probably don't want to over tune these such that they are better than AQ40 difficult to get options since you get so much CC rep when farming AQ40 (so you get them for essentially free). However, I think its fine if they are better than BWL options, or the easier to get AQ40 options. In order to be exhalted with CC you are either already in AQ40 quite a bit (meaning you probably have BWL on farm), or you have spent very large amounts of time farming CC rep, and/or running AQ20.

Making all raid gear a linear step above the solo obtainable gear only encourages a "raid-log" only environment which is one of the things (among many) that killed later retail expansions IMO.

You need to leave it such that progression through early raids is still necessary for filling in SOME slots, so that those raids are not irrelevant, but also leave it such that those that can invest time and research into finding obscure or difficult solo/grind obtainable items might still have a slight advantage over the simple raid-logger in the various tiers of progression.

Having a very few rare dungeon drops, or arduous grind items BIS even into naxx is healthy for the game IMO.

author: Elisleris
subject: Re: Midpatch Itemization Changes Preliminary Changelog
content_md:
I did some research regarding spell power amount on caster weapons in dependans of item level.
There are list of epic one-handed weapons with item level > 67 from wowhead classic.
Link: [https://www.wowhead.com/classic/items/w ... ems;0-2+20](https://www.wowhead.com/classic/items/weapons/min-level:67/max-level:99/quality:4/type:15:0:4:7?filter=51;1;30#items;0-2+20)
Each item level more than 60 increases SP about 4 per lvl , e.g.
 70 item lvl = 10*4= 40 SP
 78 item lvl = 18*4 = 72 SP
 81 item lvl = 21*4 = 84 SP
 83 item lvl = 23*4= 96 SP
Usually weapons from list have that amount of SP

Regarding our weapons from AQ20:
 74 item lvl caster weapon should has about 14*4=56 SP
For Mage all is Ok
For Paladin and Druid need increase to 56 SP
For Warlock 71 SP is near 78 item lvl weapon
For Shaman 68 SP is 77 item lvl weapon - that lvl weapons drops from AQ40 / BWL or from R14

I think the team does not put enough thought into the ramifications of changing items haphazardly. When you nerf a craftable item it nullifies peoples time and gold spent into crafting the item. When you change raid loot it nullfies peoples investment into the raid and gear they have spent weeks/months farming.

I think the final thing that doesn't get mentioned enough is that if you just change TOO MUCH stuff you waste peoples future time. Time spent farming an item that they knew from vanilla to be worthwhile to find that when it finally drops that it actually isn't the item they know anymore at all. These kind of changes aren't as bad on raid loot when you are working with a large group to farm them and have the hive mind of your guild to let you know when you're after an item that has changed. What really hurts is when you start changing a bunch of random dungeon gear, especially nerfing like the example of boreal mantle further up in the discussion, so that someone might invest a ton of time to ultimately be let down.

I'd suggest if heavy handed changes/nerfs continue that a directory is created documenting every item change on the server to look up quickly and analyze. And if that seems like too daunting of a task to do, maybe consider that you are changing too much stuff.

To start with, thinking about it, there's probably no real good reason to nerf Boreal since frost dps is already pretty low. But in the sense of gear progression, it'd probably feel good. Because, I dunno if you play mage or not and if you've geared up into AQ40, but going `down` in terms of gear power when you spec fire into AQ40 is lame. Boreal Mantle is not a fun item how it is, and, likewise, Bloodvine, turban was not fun -- Boreal was also a "catch-up" item that got buffed in 1.10. Blues being *considerably* better than epics is kinda unfun. When I was gearing, you literally skip all of tier 1 and tier 2 because greens/blues/crafted are better. You get pre-raid bis and there's like 4? items you even want from MC. (I'm thinking mana igniting cord, toep, choker, wep, maybe t2 pants). And if turtle hadn't buffed the quest rewards, there was nothing at all you wanted from Ony.

Which, imo, is the same problem with making Netherwind shoulders the second best in the game. There's literally no point in getting tier 2.5 then. And t3 only after you're juggling hit cap.

As an aside, my guess is that Blizzard intentionally made mage t2.5/3 weaker relative to warlock because of the hit talents. EDIT: What I mean is, they were trying to balance mage and warlock dps by tweaking their sets accordingly. But since warlocks are top ranged dps on twow, you don't need to worry about it :p

author: Dragunovi
subject: 1.17.1 Itemization Changelog
content_md:
Greetings! Here's the itemization changelog detailing all item related additions and changes coming in **Patch 1.17.1: Labor and Legacy**.

The list might seem a bit small but that's due to the majority of changes planned for this patch being pushed forward with the Midpatch Itemization Changes that happened sometime after the release of Patch 1.17.0.

 **Keep in mind that the changes and additions are subject to change and not final.**

 **Item Additions**
- Added 16 drops for the new rares found in Blackstone Island, Thalassian Highlands and Forlorn Summit.

- Added 7 new crafting recipes for the new starting zones: Maritime Gumbo, Gloves of Manathirst, Blast Shield, Volatile Concoction, Unstable Mining Dynamite, Lynxstep Boots and Enchant 2H Weapon - Minor Intellect.

- Added many junk drops to Thalassian Highlands.

- Added something fanatical to C'thun.

- Added Aspect of Seradane to Solnius.
 **Item Adjustments**
- Obsidian Mail Tunic now reduces spell damage taken by 3% instead of a flat 10 damage.

- Sigil of Penetration and Invocation of Shattering now grant 40 Armor Penetration down from 75.

- Invocation enchants from Lower Karazhan Halls should now function properly without needing a dedicated fix patch.

- Totem of Flowing Water's mana return has been buffed from 10 to 25.

- Totem of the Endless Flicker now has a new effect: "Increases the duration of your Flame Shock by 3 sec."

- Totem of the Calming Water now grants 8 MP5 instead of 5 MP5 and additionally grants 10 more mana when your Water Shield is struck.

- Idol of Evergrowth now has a new effect: "Your Thorns additionally gives a 3% chance when attacked to inflict 15-20 Nature damage to nearby enemies."

- Libram of Truth now has a new effect: "Your Devotion Aura additionally reduces all physical damage taken 2%."

- Staff of the Qiraji Prophets now grants you 3% Spell Hit when its effect is procced instead of 50 Spell Penetration, but its proc chance has been reduced from 25% to 15%.

- Drake Talon Cleaver's proc rate has been increased from 1 to 2 procs per minute.

- Neretzek, The Blood Drinker's proc rate has been increased from 0.8 to 1.4 procs per minute.

- Hyperchromatic Deflector and Towerforge Battlegear's 3 Set Bonus now has a 3% chance to reflect spells down from 5%.

- Thornpod's range has been reduced from 20 to 8 yards and now scales 0.05 from Spellpower down from 1.

- Chromie's Broken Pocket Watch's spell proc now properly reduces casting speed, the old stats have been restored and the description updated to be clearer.

- Fixed incorrect armor and block values on some low level custom items.

- Renamed the trinket version of Shard of Eternity to Temporal Anomaly to prevent confusion.
 **Emerald Sanctum Loot and Loottable Adjustments**

- Normal Mode Loot:
 - Fixed slightly off armor values for most pieces, netting an overall increase in armor.
 - Increased item level from 76 to 78, increasing overall power.

 - Robe of the Dreamways: 44 -> 46 Spellpower

 - Jadestone Helmet: 16 -> 18 Agility, 15 -> 16 Strength

 - Staff of the Dreamer: 106 -> 121 Healing Power, 4 -> 5 MP5

 - Shard of Nightmare: 36 -> 37 Spellpower

 - Veil of Nightmare: 30 -> 32 Attack Power

 - Sandals of Lucidity: 16 -> 18 Stamina, 17 -> 18 Intellect

 - Sanctum Bark Wraps: 14 -> 15 Agility, 13 -> 14 Stamina

 - Talonwind Gauntlets: 20 -> 22 Agility

 - Mantle of the Wakener: 26 -> 28 Spellpower

 - Mallet of the Awakening: 10 -> 11 Stamina, Increased DPS from 57.5 to 59.9

 - Scaleshield of Emerald Flight: 11 -> 12 All Stats

 - Ancient Jade Leggings: Added 9 Strength

 - Axe of Dormant Slumber: 8 -> 9 Strength, Increased DPS from 58.2 to 59.8

 - Ring of Nature's Duality: 51 -> 40 Healing Power, Replaced 1% Spell Hit with 1% Spell Crit (Hopefully the last change on this item.)

- Hardmode Loot:
 - Increased item level from 78 to 81, increasing overall power.

 - Choker of the Emerald Lord: 27 -> 28 Spellpower, 11 -> 12 Nature Resist, Added 1% Spell Hit

 - Crystal Sword of the Blossom: Increased DPS from 59.4 to 62.9

 - Naturecaller's Tunic: 18 -> 20 Stamina, 20 -> 21 Intellect, 13 -> 25 Spirit

 - Nature's Call: 5 -> 8 Stamina, Increased DPS from 46.8 to 49.0

 - Jadestone Protector: 12 -> 13 Intellect, 15 -> 18 Extra Block Value

 - Breath of Solnius: 10 -> 11 Spirit

- Claw of Erennius Quest Rewards:
 - Rewards buffed from Item Level 66 to 74, increasing stats alongside it.

 - Jadestone Skewer: 35 -> 39 Agility, Increased DPS from 62.6 to 72.8 and Feral Attack Power from 84 to 196

 - Jadestone Mallet: 8 -> 10 Stamina, 6 -> 13 Spirit, 68 -> 106 Healing Power

 - Claw of Senthos: 20 -> 24 Attack Power, Increased DPS from 48.1 to 56.0
In addition to the loot changes, the Solnius and Favor of Erennius (Hardmode Reward Chest) have seen adjustments, even completely redoing Solnius' loottable. Here are the notable changes:
- Smoldering Dream Essence, which is needed for the Druid's Emerald Blessing, now has a 35% chance to drop up from 20%.

- Solnius and Favor of Erennius are now guaranteed to drop a Fading Dream Fragment but Solnius no longer drops Small Dream Shards. This should make his overall Dream Shard net not luck dependant and overall higher if you can clear him in Hardmode.

- Bag of the Vast Conscious now has a 25% chance to drop instead of 15% chance from Solnius and you are now guaranteed a Bag of the Vast Conscious from the Favor of Erennius.

- Solnius' gear drop loot groups are now split into three which consist of the Physical, Magical and Weapon/Relic categories, making sure that he's unable to roll multiple of the same items from the same kill. This adjustment also fixes the edge cases where he had a very rare chance to not drop an item from one of the loot groups.

- Solnius is now guaranteed to drop a Dreamscale up from 48% chance.

- Enchant Gloves - Nature Power is now properly part of the crafting recipes loot group.

- Formula: Eternal Dreamstone Shard now has a 1% chance to drop, up from 0.85% chance.
 **Crafting Recipe Adjustments**
- Arcanite Belt Buckle's Arcanite Bar cost has been reduced from 8 to 3.

subject: 1.17.2 Preliminary Itemization Changelog
content_md:
Greetings! Here's the **preliminary** itemization changelog detailing all item related additions and changes coming in **Patch 1.17.2: Tower of Karazhan.**

This list will be updated as more changes are done or revised, so keep in mind that these changes are subject to change. Check back here often so you don't miss anything!

 **Summary:**
- We've taken a second look at all of the Gilneas City loot and increased the power of most gear to make the dungeon worth running even without quests.

- We've turned the dial back slightly on most of the Moroes drops.

- Made most of the underperforming caster staves in tiers below Naxxramas more worthwhile to use.

- Adjusted quite a few dungeon drops, especially changing Uncommon items in dungeons at or above level 40 to be Rare quality and buffed accordingly.

- Buffed reputation rewards for Warsong Gulch and Arathi Basin, making the grind much more worthwhile.

- Buffed Atiesh for Priest to have spellpower equal to Warlock and Mage, and Atiesh for Druid to have more feral attack power, changed the aura granted to be useful for all roles and added spellpower similiar to the Priest version.
 **Stat Adjustments**:
- Meditation's stat budget has seen a lookover. In simple terms: Some items should see a small nerf while some items should see an overall buff from this change. If a Meditation item is not listed in the stat specific changelog section below then the item is unchanged.

- Resillience is seeing a complete rework. Instead of reducing your chance to be critically struck, it will instead reduce the damage of critical strikes and damage over time effects on you, making it much more oriented for PvP combat, as it was mostly utilized by PvE tanks to get rid of critical strikes from bosses.

 **The conversion rate is:** 1% reduced chance to get critically struck is turned into 3% reduced damage from critical strikes and damage over time effects. To avoid any confusion, anything in the changelog that lists resillience as 3% is for the new version of the stat, equal to 1% of the old version.

Please keep in mind that this change will go live alongside other class centric changes such as the addition of the Alternative Tier Sets and the second batch of Class Changes, don't look at this in a vacuum.
 **Item Adjustments**

- Staff of Dominance: Intellect reduced from 37 to 34, Spellpower increased from 40 to 53.

- Staff of the Qiraji Prophets: Intellect reduced from 26 to 22, Spellpower increased from 56 to 72.

- Shadow Wing Focus Staff: Intellect reduced from 40 to 32, Spellpower increased from 56 to 72, Added 1% Spell Hit.

- Band of Servitude: Spellpower increased from 23 to 27, Stamina reduced from 8 to 5, Intellect reduced from 9 to 5.

- Ring of the Academy: Spellpower reduced from 16 to 12.

- Epaulets of the Forgotten Past: Replaced 6 Defense with 18 Spellpower, reduced MP5 from 4 to 3.

- Visor of Command: The strength aura's range has been increased from 20 to 35 yards, and no longer gets overriden by other strength buffs.

- Blackfire Orb and Orb of Kaladoon: Now has 1% Haste and 15 Spellpower.

- Refined Plague Strain: Now instantly applied when used, the use range has been increased from 5 to 30 yards, now has 5% spellpower scaling and (hopefully) should properly damage targets within 8 yards of the initial target too.

- Scythe of the Harvest: Procs Per Minute reduced from 3 to 2, but now grants 16 Strength.

- Idol of the Emerald Rot: Damage increased from "90 to 131" to "150 to 191" damage, and the Poison Bolt is now guaranteed to land.

- Harmonious Gauntlets: Increased all stats from 5 to 8, reduced Healing Power from 51 to 42.

- Peacekeeper Gauntlets: Increased Stamina from 7 to 8, increased MP5 from 4 to 6, reduced Healing Power from 59 to 51. These two gauntlets were reduced in healing power to compensate for the increase coming with the new Holy Paladin talent Ironclad.

- Bracelets of Royal Redemption: Increased all stats by 1, reduced Healing Power from 53 to 46.

- Might of Menethil: Now grants 406 Feral Attack Power.

- Dream's Herald: Proc's attack speed reduction no longer stacks with similiar effects.

- Libram of the Dreamguard: Reduced amount of Holy Shield charges granted from 2 to 1.

- Breath of Solnius: Now has a 15 second internal cooldown (equal to its duration to prevent re-triggering before the duration is finished.), and multi-target heals only count as one instance of healing in terms of proc chance.

- Jadestone Protector: Replaced 1% Resillience with 1% Block. Increased Defense from 8 to 9.

- Gold Ore: Now uses the proper Gold Ore icon instead of reusing the Copper Ore icon.

- Wing of the Time-Lord: Haste reduced from 2% to 1%.

- Bonereaver's Edge: Procs per minute returned to original Vanilla value, reducing it from 3 to 2.

- Chromie's Broken Pocket Watch: The triggered effect is now a Physical debuff instead of a buff.

- Scale of the Red Drake: Added 10 Fire Resistance, buffed Fire Spellpower from 14 to 19.

- Biznicks 247x128 Accurascope: Changed enchant text from "+3% Hit" to "Scope (+3% Ranged Hit)". This is only a description update to make it clear that this enchant only increases ranged hit chance, functionality remains unchanged from Vanilla.

- **New Item Set:** Possessions of the Lost. Perhaps the long dead should be disturbed after all.

- Eye of Diminution: Spell critical chance increased from 2% to 3%.

- Atiesh (Priest): Spellpower increased from 120 to 150 to be on par with the other full spellpower versions.

- Atiesh (Druid): Class special aura changed from 11 MP5 to 2% Haste. Feral Attack Power increased from 420 to 600. Now also grants 150 Spellpower similiar to the Priest version.

- Spinal Reaper: Mana granted increased from 150 to 300.

- Warmth of Forgiveness: Increased mana granted on use from 500 to 700.

- Libram of Divinity/Totem of Sustaining and Libram of Light/Totem of Life: Healing reduced from 53 to 28 for the former two and healing reduced from 83/80 to 41/40.

This change was done because the effect implies that this effect functions like healing power obeying coefficients, while these effects actually functioned as flat healing increase, after this these relics should increase healing by approximately the original intended amount displayed on the items. In short terms, this made these items be slightly more than double in power, equalling around 123 healing power for the rare relics and around 189 healing power for the epic ones. To prevent further confusion around these items we've removed the "up to" text from these items to fully represent they are flat healing increases.

- Fey Dreamcatcher: Now grants 5% Meditation and 6 Spirit passively instead of an active on use HoT.

- Ring of Forlorn Spirits: Reduced Spirit from 7 to 2.

- Feymist Robe: Increased Spirit from 10 to 12.

- Sandals of Inner Peace: Reduced Spirit from 15 to 13.

- Isle Watcher's Sash: Replaced 3 Agility with 3 Spirit.

- Green Dragonscale Breastplate: Reduced Spirit from 21 to 19.

- Green Dragonscale Gauntlets: Reduced Spirit from 18 to 17, reduced Meditation from 5% to 4%.

- Green Dragonscale Leggings: Reduced Spirit from 22 to 20.

- Leggings of Arcana: Reduced Spirit from 30 to 28.

- Cowl of Mivax: Reduced Spirit from 24 to 21.

- Dreambreeze Cowl: Increased Spirit from 14 to 17.

- Mantle of Twisted Damnation: Increased Shadow Spellpower from 14 to 24, increased Intellect from 16 to 18.

- Memento of the Lost: Increased Spirit from 19 to 21.

- Shroud of Haunted Torment: Removed 2% Haste.

- Verdant Dreamer's Breastplate: Reduced Intellect from 18 to 16.

- Vestments of Eternal Autumn: Increased Intellect from 12 to 16, increased Stamina from 8 to 15, increased Spirit from 20 to 24, increased Meditation from 5% to 7%.

- Verdant Eye Necklace: Removed 6 Stamina.

- Staff of the Dreamer: Increased Healing Power from 121 to 134.

- Pendant of Forgotten Names: Now grants 10% Meditation instead of MP5.

- Ring of Spiritual Fervor: Now grants 10% Meditation instead of MP5, replaced 11 Stamina with 11 Spirit.
 **Royal Seals of Eldre'thalas**
- Mage: Now grants 23 Spellpower instead of 8 MP5.

- Priest: Now grants 18 Spellpower, 15 Healing Power and 4 MP5.

- Druid and Shaman: Now grants 23 Spellpower and 22 Healing Power.

- Hunter: Now grants 38 Attack Power and 10 Ranged Attack Power.

- Warrior: Now grants 30 Attack Power and 8 Defense.

- Paladin: Now grants 18 Spellpower, 15 Healing Power and 8 Defense.

- Warlock and Rogue are unchanged.
 **Lower Karazhan Halls**
- Rod of Resuscitation: 25 Intellect -> 23 Intellect ; 25 Stamina -> 24 Stamina

- Cloudplate Wristguards: 17 Stamina -> 16 Stamina ; 13 SP -> 11 SP ; 356 Armor -> 346 Armor

- Anasterian's Legacy: 57-104 Damage -> 54-101 Damage ; 12 Agiity -> 9 Agility

- Breastplate of Earthen Might: 44 Attack Power -> 36 Attack Power ; 458 Armor -> 446 Armor

- Leggings of the Inferno: 22 Agiity -> 20 Agiity

- Vest of Encroaching Darkness: 39 Spellpower -> 35 Spellpower

- Fist of the Forgotten Order: 194-297 Damage -> 190-293 Damage

 **Dungeon Loot Buffs:**

 **Gilneas City:**

- Greymane Vambraces: 2 Strength -> 6 Strength, 4 Spirit -> 5 Spirit

- Greymane Gauntlets: Added 7 Strength, 5 Spirit and 6 Stamina.

- Regal Goldforged Breastplate: 14 Agility -> 19 Agility, 14 Intellect -> 8 Intellect

 **Razorfen Downs:**

>
> - Warmth of Forgiveness: Increased mana granted on use from 500 to 700.

Opinion of a healer (shaman) here:

 1. Breath of Solnius is by far our best trinket. If ES is supposed to be on par with BWL/AQ gear, then you shouldn't nerf it to be barely better than Jed's trinket from UBRS. That proc rate still bad*. Nerf it so that can't proc off the bounces, that's fine. But don't put an internal cooldown on it at all. The trinket becomes fully trivial, and then at this point you're looking at all healers now needing the same 2 trinkets in order to be full BiS: Rejuv Gem and Eye of the Dead

 2. If you want to make Warmth an actual useable item, because it's basically a tiny bit better than Shard of the Scale right now, you may want to add some +healing on it (from a healer POV). If Rejuv Gem has very high +heal and fair mp5, then make Warmth have fair +healing and very high mp5 (with on-use effect). Something like +50 healing on it could definitely make it an option for some healers and would diversify itemization. Nordranaar Teas are extremely strong, so mp5 and on-use mana gain are less of a need, so yeah, the +heal on Warmth would need to be pretty high to make it valuable.

 *Edit, I noticed you lowered rom 45s to 15s internal cooldown but it still makes the trinket weak considering there's only a 5% chance to proc altogether. Make it a 20% chance to proc to compensate, at the very least

The point that I believe has been sorely missed by everyone responding to me is "Why is Meditation even a stat at all?"

It performs the exact same function as MP5, increases mana regeneration while casting. It's just harder for the devs to tune because instead of being completely linear, it becomes a moving target where you can accumulate a critical mass of mana regen if they slip up.

If Mp5 is a weak stat, the solution isn't to supplant it with a new stat that accomplishes the same function. The solution is to fundamentally question how much Mp5 is consuming the itemization budget of items with it and buff the items accordingly.

Mp5 & meditation have fundamentally different target audiences. Each class has a different spirit to mana conversion. Whereas mp5 is static in all aspects.

Meditation at least offers you some interesting considrrations in gameplay & gearing as its value changes depending on class and playstile (if you stopcast a bunch, you regularly fall out of the 5 second rule and gain no benefit from meditation for short amounts of time)

It also offers tradeoff where either more meditation or more raw spirit can be better at various breakpoints.

Whereas mp5 is completely uninterractable and boring

author: Yzzzzzz
subject: Re: 1.17.2 Preliminary Itemization Changelog
content_md:
Breath of Solnius: Now has a 15 second internal cooldown (equal to its duration to prevent re-triggering before the duration is finished.), and multi-target heals only count as one instance of healing in terms of proc chance.

I believe the nerf to the "Breath of Solnius" trinket is a bit excessive. The base stats of 30 Healing and 11 Spirit are not particularly powerful. If the proc is modified to have a 15-second internal cooldown and can only trigger with a 5% chance, the uptime for the Haste effect will be very low. For healers, trinkets with an unstable proc and low uptime are of limited usefulness. I suggest that if you modify the internal cooldown and adjust the proc mechanism, you should compensate by increasing the proc chance. This would ensure that the trinket's uptime remains at a reasonable level.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: 1.17.2 Preliminary Itemization Changelog
content_md:
With a 5% chance to proc breath, you need 20 casts on average to get one.
In the best case scenario of using 1.5 second cast heals, that means on average you spend 30 seconds casting to trigger it for an effect that lasts 15 seconds. So the uptime is ~33%. Thats an average of 6.7% haste from one itemslot on top of other stats.

But most healers will be using slower heals especially considering during breaths active you want to use slower heals too. Considering otherwise you loose the value from haste to the gcd. With a 2.5 second cast heal (for instance chainheal or holy light) the number goes down to 4.6% haste.

Still very very strong, but it curbstomps whats fun about the trinket. I suggest instead to remove the addheal & statd as well as the cd on the trinket (and keep it proc only once for aoe spells) that way gain between ~10% average haste on a very idealistic scenario and 6-7% average haste in a more realistic setting.

Its still a very potent trinket, but its still a healer trinket that isnt exactly reliable. And that itself is a downside on a role that id all about reliability

Opinion of a healer (shaman) here:

1. Breath of Solnius is by far our best trinket. If ES is supposed to be on par with BWL/AQ gear, then you shouldn't nerf it to be barely better than Jed's trinket from UBRS.
